title: Credit Card Validator
spec: Write a Python script with a function `validate_credit_card(number_str)` and a `main()` driver. The function must strip all spaces and dashes from the input. It should first check if the string is entirely numeric and between 13 and 16 digits long. Next, identify the issuer: return 'Visa' if it starts with 4, 'MasterCard' if it starts with 51-55, and 'Amex' if it starts with 34 or 37, returning 'Unknown' otherwise. Finally, implement the Luhn algorithm: reverse the digits, double every second digit, subtract 9 if a doubled value is greater than 9, sum all resulting digits, and verify the total modulo 10 is 0. Return a tuple of `(is_valid_boolean, issuer_string)`.

title: Vending Machine Change Dispenser
spec: Implement a script with `calculate_change(price, paid, inventory)` and a short `main()` function to test it. Convert all inputs to integer cents immediately to avoid floating-point errors. The `inventory` is a dictionary of coin/bill denominations in cents (2000, 1000, 500, 100, 25, 10, 5, 1) to their available quantities. If `paid` is less than `price`, raise a ValueError. Otherwise, iterate from the largest denomination to the smallest, greedily deducting from the inventory and adding to a `change_given` dictionary until the exact change is met. If the inventory lacks the necessary coins to make exact change, raise a RuntimeError. Return the `change_given` dictionary.

title: Ten-Pin Bowling Scorer
spec: Write a module with `score_bowling(throws)` and a `main()` driver to evaluate a game of ten-pin bowling. The input `throws` is a list of integers representing knocked down pins (0-10) for the entire game. Iterate through exactly 10 frames. If a frame is a strike (10 pins on the first throw), the score for that frame is 10 plus the next two throws. If it is a spare (two throws summing to 10), the score is 10 plus the next one throw. Open frames simply sum the two throws. Ensure the logic properly tracks the index in the throws list, especially for the 10th frame which may have up to 3 throws. Return the final integer score.

title: Tax Bracket Calculator
spec: Create a script featuring `calculate_income_tax(income, status)` and a `main()` block. First, deduct a standard deduction based on `status`: 12000 for 'single' and 24000 for 'married'. If the resulting taxable income is 0 or less, the tax is 0. Otherwise, apply a progressive tax rate: the first 10,000 of taxable income is taxed at 10%, the next 30,000 at 12%, the next 50,000 at 22%, and any remaining amount at 24%. Finally, if the original gross income exceeds 100,000, add a flat 1,000 high-earner surcharge. Return the final calculated tax as a float.

title: RPN Stack Calculator
spec: Implement an RPN (Reverse Polish Notation) evaluator `evaluate_rpn(expression)` alongside a `main()` testing function. The input is a space-separated string of numbers and operators. Split the string and process tokens using a list as a stack. If a token is a number, push it as a float. If it is '+', '-', '*', or '/', pop the top two numbers, apply the operation, and push the result, explicitly raising ZeroDivisionError for division by zero. Support three special commands: 'DUP' duplicates the top item, 'SWAP' swaps the top two items, and 'DROP' removes the top item. After processing all tokens, return the single remaining item on the stack.

title: Poker Hand Evaluator
spec: Write a script containing `evaluate_poker_hand(cards)` and a `main()` function. The input `cards` is a list of 5 strings, like ['10H', 'JH', 'QH', 'KH', 'AH']. Parse the ranks and suits, mapping face cards (J, Q, K, A) to integers 11, 12, 13, and 14. Sort the ranks to easily check for consecutive values (a Straight). Check if all suits are identical (a Flush). Count the frequencies of each rank to identify pairs, three-of-a-kind, or four-of-a-kind. Evaluate these properties to return the highest possible hand ranking string, such as 'Straight Flush', 'Four of a Kind', 'Full House', 'Flush', or 'Pair'.

title: Password Strength Analyzer
spec: Create a script with `assess_password(password)` and a `main()` testing driver to generate a security score from 0 to 100. Initialize the score at 0. Add 10 points if the length is at least 8, and an additional 10 points if it is 12 or more. Add 15 points each for containing at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit, and one special character. Apply a 20-point penalty if the password consists entirely of letters or entirely of digits. Apply a 15-point penalty if it contains common substrings like '123' or 'password' (case-insensitive). Clamp the final score so it never falls below 0 or exceeds 100, and return it.

title: IPv4 Subnet Calculator
spec: Write a script with `subnet_info(ip_str, cidr)` and a `main()` block. Parse the IPv4 string into four octets and convert it into a single 32-bit integer. Calculate the 32-bit subnet mask based on the integer `cidr` prefix (e.g., 24). Apply a bitwise AND between the IP and the mask to determine the network address. Apply a bitwise OR between the IP and the inverted mask to calculate the broadcast address. Determine the number of usable hosts, which is 2^(32-cidr) - 2 (handle edge cases where cidr >= 31 by returning 0). Convert the network and broadcast integers back to dot-decimal strings, returning them and the host count in a dictionary.

title: Text Justification Engine
spec: Implement `justify_text(words, max_width)` with a `main()` driver to format paragraphs. Iterate through the words, packing as many as possible into a line without exceeding `max_width` (including at least one space between words). For each completed line except the last, calculate the total missing spaces and distribute them evenly among the gaps between words. If the spaces cannot be divided evenly, distribute the remainder starting from the leftmost gaps. The very last line of the text must be left-justified with single spaces, padded with trailing spaces up to the width. Return a list of the formatted line strings.

title: E-commerce Checkout Pipeline
spec: Write a module with `process_checkout(cart_items, state_code)` and a `main()` test function. `cart_items` is a list of dictionaries with keys: 'name', 'price', 'category', and 'quantity'. First, calculate line item totals. If an item's category is 'electronics', apply a 10% discount to it. If the category is 'apparel', apply a 'buy 2 get 1 free' logic to the quantity. Sum the adjusted prices to get a subtotal. Calculate shipping: flat 15.00, but free if the subtotal is over 75.00. Finally, apply state sales tax to the subtotal plus shipping: 8% for 'CA', 7% for 'NY', and 0% for others. Return the rounded final grand total.

title: Time Zone Meeting Scheduler
spec: Create a script with `find_meeting_slot(utc_hours, participant_offsets)` and a `main()` driver. `utc_hours` is a list of integers (0-23) representing proposed meeting times in UTC. `participant_offsets` is a list of integers representing local time zone offsets (e.g., -8, 0, 9). For every proposed UTC hour, loop through the offsets to calculate the local hour for each participant, wrapping around 24 hours using modulo arithmetic. A meeting slot is considered valid only if the local time for ALL participants falls within standard working hours (9 to 17, inclusive). Return the first valid UTC hour found, or None if no proposed time works.

title: Chess Knight Minimum Path
spec: Implement a module with `knight_moves(start_pos, end_pos)` and a `main()` driver. The inputs are standard algebraic chess notation strings like 'a1' and 'h8'. Convert these strings into (x, y) coordinates where both axes range from 0 to 7. Use a Breadth-First Search (BFS) queue to find the shortest path. Track visited coordinates in a set to avoid infinite loops. In each BFS step, generate all 8 possible L-shaped knight moves, discarding any that fall outside the 0-7 board boundaries. Return the integer representing the minimum number of moves required to reach the destination.

title: Log File Anomaly Detector
spec: Write a script featuring `detect_anomalies(log_lines)` and a `main()` test function. `log_lines` is a list of comma-separated strings: 'timestamp, level, user_id, action' (where timestamp is an integer). Skip any line where the level is 'INFO'. Track sequential 'FAILED' actions per user using a dictionary. If a user hits 3 FAILED actions in a row, generate a 'Brute Force' alert string for them. If a user registers a FAILED action followed by a 'SUCCESS' action, check the timestamps; if the difference is 60 or less, generate a 'Compromised' alert. Return a list of all generated alert strings.

title: Conway Game of Life Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(grid)` to evolve a cellular automaton. The input is a list of lists of integers representing a grid of cells where zero is dead and one is alive. For each step, a living cell with two or three living neighbors survives. A dead cell with exactly three living neighbors becomes alive. All other cells die or remain dead. The function should advance the grid by ten steps and return the final grid state. The grid edges do not wrap around, so cells outside the bounds are always dead.

title: Base Sixty Four Encoder
spec: Write a function `encode(data)` to convert a byte sequence into a text string using base sixty four encoding. Process the bytes in groups of three. Convert each group into a twenty four bit integer. Split this integer into four six bit segments. Map each segment to a character using the standard uppercase, lowercase, digit, plus, and slash alphabet. If the input length is not a multiple of three, pad the output with one or two equals signs at the end. For example, processing the letters c, a, and t outputs the characters Y, 2, F, and 0.

title: Markdown to HTML Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(text)` to convert a simple formatted text string into standard web tags. If a line starts with a hash symbol and a space, wrap the rest of the line in a level one heading tag. If a line starts with a dash and a space, it belongs to an unordered list. Group consecutive list items into a single unordered list tag and wrap each item in list item tags. Wrap any other non empty line in paragraph tags. Find words surrounded by double asterisks and wrap them in bold tags. Return the combined output as a single string.

title: Least Recently Used Cache Simulation
spec: Write a function `cache(requests)` to simulate a memory cache with a maximum capacity of four items. The input is a list of integer item identifiers accessed over time. Maintain a collection of currently cached items. When a requested item is not in the collection, record a cache miss and add the item. If the collection is full, remove the item that was accessed longest ago. When an item is already present, record a cache hit and mark it as most recently used. Return a tuple containing the total number of hits and the total number of misses.

title: A-Star Grid Pathfinding
spec: Write a function `navigate(maze)` to find the shortest path from the top left corner to the bottom right corner of a grid. The input is a list of lists of integers where zero is an open space and one is a wall. Use a pathfinding algorithm that prioritizes nodes based on the distance traveled plus the Manhattan distance to the goal. Keep track of visited coordinates and the lowest cost to reach each cell. Allow movement up, down, left, and right. Return a list of coordinate tuples representing the shortest path, or an empty list if no path exists.

title: Robust CSV Parser
spec: Write a function `delimit(text)` to parse a text string containing comma separated values into a list of lists of strings. Fields are separated by commas and rows are separated by newline characters. A field may be enclosed in double quotes. While inside quotes, commas and newlines are treated as regular characters, not separators. Two consecutive double quotes inside a quoted field represent a single literal double quote. Ignore any spaces outside of quotes. Return the structured list of rows.

title: Roman Numeral Arithmetic
spec: Write a function `calculate(expression)` to evaluate a text string containing an addition or subtraction of two Roman numerals. First, convert both Roman numerals into integers. Remember that smaller symbols before larger symbols mean subtraction, like four or nine. Perform the requested arithmetic operation. Then, convert the resulting integer back into a Roman numeral using the standard symbols from one to one thousand. Return the final numeral string. For example, adding X and V returns XV.

title: Darts Match Scorer
spec: Write a function `darts(throws)` to calculate the remaining score for a player in a game of five hundred and one. The input is a list of text strings representing dart throws, such as single twenty, double twenty, or triple twenty. Subtract the value of each throw from the current score. A player must reach exactly zero points, and the final winning throw must be a double or the inner bullseye. If a throw reduces the score to one point, or below zero, the entire turn of up to three darts is busted and the score reverts to the value at the start of that turn. Return the final integer score.

title: Graph Topological Sort
spec: Write a function `resolve(dependencies)` to order a set of tasks based on their prerequisites. The input is a list of pairs where the first item must be completed before the second item. Count how many prerequisites each task has. Find all tasks with zero prerequisites and add them to a processing queue. Repeatedly take a task from the queue, append it to an output list, and reduce the prerequisite count for any tasks that depend on it. If their count reaches zero, add them to the queue. Return the ordered list of tasks, or an empty list if a cycle prevents completion.

title: Run Length Encoding
spec: Write a function `runlength(data)` to compress a text string by replacing consecutive identical characters with a count followed by the character. Iterate through the string and count repetitions. Because the count must fit in a single byte, if a sequence repeats more than two hundred fifty five times, split it into multiple blocks. To avoid ambiguity with numbers in the original text, only apply the count if a character repeats three or more times; otherwise, output the characters exactly as they appear. Return the compressed string.

title: List Difference Algorithm
spec: Write a function `compare(original, modified)` to determine the sequence of additions and deletions needed to transform one list of strings into another. First, build a two dimensional grid to find the length of the longest common subsequence between the two lists. Fill the grid by comparing items at each position. Then, trace backwards from the bottom right corner of the grid to reconstruct the exact changes. Prepend a plus sign for added items, a minus sign for removed items, and a space for unchanged items. Return the list of annotated strings.

title: Soundex Phonetic Encoding
spec: Write a function `soundex(word)` to convert an English word into a four character phonetic code. Retain the first letter of the word in uppercase. Map the remaining consonants to digits based on phonetic similarity, grouping similar sounds like the letters b, f, p, and v together into the number one. Ignore vowels, the letter y, the letter h, and the letter w. If two adjacent letters have the same number, or are separated only by an h or w, keep only one number. Stop when the code reaches four characters. If it is too short, pad it with zeros. Return the final text string.

title: Segmented Sieve of Eratosthenes
spec: Write a function `primes(limit)` to find all prime numbers up to a given maximum limit using a segmented approach to save memory. First, find all basic prime numbers up to the square root of the limit. Create a boolean array for small chunks of the overall range. For each chunk, use the basic primes to cross out multiples within that specific range. Collect the remaining unmarked numbers as they are prime. Continue this process chunk by chunk until the maximum limit is reached. Return a list of all discovered prime numbers.

title: Book Identifier Validator
spec: Write a function `verify(code)` to check if a text string is a valid thirteen digit book identifier. Remove all hyphens and spaces from the input. Verify that the resulting text contains exactly thirteen digits. Multiply each digit by a weight, alternating between one for the first digit, three for the second, one for the third, and so on. Sum all these products together. The identifier is valid if the total sum is a multiple of ten. Return a boolean value indicating true if it is valid or false otherwise.

title: Dictionary Based Compression
spec: Write a function `lzw(text)` to reduce the size of a text string using dictionary based compression. Initialize a dictionary mapping all single characters to their standard integer codes. Read through the text while building the longest possible sequence of characters that already exists in the dictionary. When a sequence is found that is not in the dictionary, output the integer code for the known part. Then, add the new sequence to the dictionary with the next available integer code. Start a new sequence with the final unrecognized character. Return a list of integer codes.

title: Number Grid Puzzle Validator
spec: Write a function `validate(board)` to evaluate a nine by nine grid of integers to ensure it follows the rules of a popular number puzzle. The input is a list of nine lists, representing the rows. Zero represents an empty space. Check that every row contains unique numbers from one to nine, ignoring zeros. Check that every column also contains unique numbers. Finally, divide the grid into nine three by three subgrids and verify that each subgrid contains unique numbers. Return true if all checks pass without any duplicates, or false if a rule is violated.

title: English Word Pluralizer
spec: Write a function `pluralize(words)` to convert a list of noun strings into their plural forms based on standard spelling rules. If a word ends in s, x, z, ch, or sh, append the letters e and s. If a word ends in a consonant followed by y, replace the y with the letters i, e, and s. If a word ends in a vowel followed by y, simply add an s. If a word ends in f or fe, replace that ending with the letters v, e, and s. Otherwise, just append an s to the word. Return the list of modified strings. Assume all input strings are lowercase.

title: Elevator Dispatch Simulator
spec: Write a function `dispatch(calls)` to simulate an elevator servicing passenger requests in a ten story building. The elevator starts on the first floor moving upwards. The input is a list of requested floor numbers. The elevator must travel in its current direction as long as there are remaining requests in that direction. When it reaches a requested floor, it pauses to open its doors and removes that floor from its list. If there are no more requests ahead, it reverses direction to handle any remaining calls behind it. Return the sequence of floors visited in order.

title: Billiards Break Scorer
spec: Write a function `snooker(pots)` to calculate the total score of a billiards break. The input is a list of color strings representing the balls potted in sequence. A red ball is worth one point and must be followed by a colored ball. The colors yellow, green, brown, blue, pink, and black are worth two to seven points respectively. Keep track of the expected next ball type. If a color is potted when a red was expected, or if an invalid sequence occurs, the break ends immediately. Return the accumulated total points before any foul.

title: Polybius Square Cipher
spec: Write a function `polybius(message)` to encrypt a text string using a five by five grid of letters. First, construct the grid using the standard alphabet, combining the letters i and j into a single cell to fit twenty five slots. Convert the input message to lowercase and remove any non alphabetic characters. For each letter in the message, find its row and column index in the grid, starting from one. Replace the letter with a two digit number formed by combining the row and column numbers. Return the final sequence of numbers as a single text string.

title: Musical Note Frequency Tuner
spec: Write a function `tune(notes)` to calculate the acoustic frequency in hertz for a sequence of musical notes. The input is a list of strings like middle C four or F sharp five. Base the calculation on A four being exactly four hundred and forty hertz. Determine the semitone distance of the given note from A four by examining the letter, any sharp or flat modifiers, and the octave number. Multiply the base frequency by the twelfth root of two raised to the power of the semitone distance. Return a list of floating point frequencies.

title: Basic Type Stringifier
spec: Write a function `stringify(data)` to convert a nested data structure into a text representation without using built in serialization libraries. The input can be a combination of lists, text strings, integers, and boolean values. If the input is a text string, enclose it in double quotes and escape any internal quotes or backslashes. If the input is a boolean, return the word true or false in lowercase. If the input is a list, recursively process each item, join them with commas, and enclose the result in square brackets. Return the final formatted text.

title: Prefix Free Code Builder
spec: Write a function `huffman(text)` to generate a prefix free binary code mapping for the characters in a text string. First, count the frequency of each character. Create a leaf node for each character and add them to a priority queue sorted by frequency. Repeatedly remove the two nodes with the lowest frequencies, merge them into a new internal node with their combined frequency, and put it back in the queue. Once only one root node remains, traverse the tree to assign a zero for every left branch and a one for every right branch. Return a list of tuples containing characters and codes.

title: Card Game Hand Evaluator
spec: Write a function `score(cards)` to calculate the highest valid total for a hand of playing cards. The input is a list of strings representing card ranks, from two up to ten, plus jack, queen, king, and ace. Face cards are worth ten points. Aces are initially worth eleven points. Sum the total value of all cards in the hand. If the total exceeds twenty one, and the hand contains aces, subtract ten points for each ace one by one until the total is twenty one or less. Return the final integer score.

title: Command Line Calendar Generator
spec: Write a function `calendar(year, month)` to generate a formatted text block representing a calendar month, similar to standard command line tools. Determine the day of the week for the first day of the given month and year using a standard mathematical formula for dates. Calculate the total number of days in the month, accounting for leap years if the month is February. Build the grid row by row, padding the first row with empty spaces until the starting day. Align all numbers in columns of three characters. Return a list of strings representing the rows.

title: Computus Easter Date
spec: Calculate the Gregorian Easter Sunday for a given year using the Meeus Jones Butcher algorithm. The entry function `computus(year)` must implement the standard division steps involving the golden number, century, and various corrections for the lunar orbit. Calculate the intermediate values by finding remainders and quotients as dictated by the algorithm. Determine the month and day from these intermediate calculations, remembering that the month will be either March or April. Return a tuple containing the year, month, and day. For example, providing 2024 returns (2024, 3, 31).

title: Universal Product Code Validator
spec: Verify the structural validity of a standard twelve digit retail barcode. The function `validate(digits)` takes a string of twelve numeric characters. Extract the first eleven digits as the payload and the final digit as the provided checksum. Multiply the digits in odd positions by three and the digits in even positions by one, then sum all these products. Find the remainder of this sum when divided by ten, and subtract that from ten to get the true checksum, though a result of ten becomes zero. Return true if the calculated checksum matches the provided one, and false otherwise. For example, providing "036000291452" returns true.

title: Haversine Geographic Distance
spec: Compute the great circle distance between two points on the Earth surface using their latitude and longitude coordinates. The function `distance(points)` receives a list of two tuples, each holding the latitude and longitude in degrees. Convert all coordinates from degrees to radians by multiplying by pi and dividing by one hundred eighty. Calculate the differences in latitude and longitude, then apply the haversine formula using the sine squared of half the differences and the cosine of the latitudes. Multiply the central angle by the Earth radius of six thousand three hundred seventy one kilometers to obtain the final distance. Return the distance rounded to the nearest kilometer. For example, providing [(51.5, 0.1), (48.8, 2.3)] returns 344.

title: Tile Game Move Scorer
spec: Calculate the score of a single word played on a premium board. The function `score(placement)` accepts a list of tuples containing a character, a letter multiplier, and a word multiplier. First, determine the base value of each letter according to standard English rules where vowels are one point, rare letters like zebra or xylophone are ten, and others vary between two and eight. Multiply each letter value by its specific letter multiplier and sum them to form the base word score. Next, multiply this sum by all the word multipliers present in the placement. Finally, if the placement contains exactly seven letters, add a fifty point bonus to the total. Return the final integer score. For example, placing a seven letter word with no multipliers returns the base sum plus 50.

title: Player Rating Adjustment
spec: Update a player competitive rating based on a single match outcome using a simplified rating system. The function `update(match)` receives a tuple containing the player current rating, the opponent rating, and the outcome which is one for a win and zero for a loss. Calculate the expected probability of winning using a logistic curve based on the difference between the two ratings divided by four hundred. Determine the rating change by multiplying a fixed constant of thirty two by the difference between the actual outcome and the expected probability. Add this change to the player original rating and round to the nearest integer. Return the new rating. For example, given current rating 1500, opponent 1600, and outcome 1, it returns 1520.

title: Torrent Metadata Decoder
spec: Parse a byte string encoded in a specific length prefixed format used by peer to peer networks. The function `decode(data)` accepts a plain string containing the encoded payload. Identify the data type by looking at the first character of the current segment. If it is an integer marker, extract the digits until the end marker and convert them to a numeric value. If it is a list marker, recursively decode elements until an end marker is reached. If it is a digit, read the length prefix, skip the colon, and extract the specified number of characters as a string. Return a tuple containing the decoded object and the remaining unparsed string. For example, providing "4:spam" returns ("spam", "").

title: Stream Cipher Encryption
spec: Encrypt or decrypt a plaintext string using a classic state based stream cipher. The function `cipher(payload)` accepts a tuple containing a string key and a string message. Initialize an array of two hundred fifty six integers from zero to two hundred fifty five. Scramble this array using the key by iterating through it and swapping elements based on the key character values and an accumulating index. Once the key schedule is complete, generate a pseudo random keystream by picking elements from the array using two updating pointers. Exclusive or each character of the message with the next keystream byte and format the result as a list of integers. For example, payload with key "Secret" and message "Attack" returns a list of integers representing the ciphertext.

title: Bounding Box Overlap
spec: Calculate the intersection over union metric for two rectangular regions. The function `overlap(boxes)` takes a list of two tuples, where each tuple contains the minimum and maximum horizontal and vertical coordinates of a box on a plane. Find the coordinates of the intersection rectangle by taking the maximum of the minimums and the minimum of the maximums. If the intersection is valid, meaning its width and height are strictly positive, calculate its area. Compute the area of both original boxes by multiplying their respective widths and heights. Divide the intersection area by the sum of the original areas minus the intersection area. Return the resulting float metric.

title: Geohash Spatial Encoder
spec: Encode a geographic coordinate into a short alphanumeric string for spatial indexing. The function `encode(coordinate)` takes a tuple of latitude and longitude floats. Start with a latitude range of negative ninety to ninety and a longitude range of negative one hundred eighty to one hundred eighty. Iteratively narrow the ranges by halving them and checking which half the coordinate falls into, emitting a one bit if it is in the upper half and a zero bit otherwise. Interleave the longitude bits and latitude bits sequentially to form a binary sequence. Group the sequence into chunks of five bits and map each chunk to a character using a standard base thirty two alphabet. Return the first eight characters of the encoded string.

title: Document Keyword Scorer
spec: Calculate the relevance score of a specific keyword across a collection of text documents. The function `score(corpus)` receives a tuple holding a target word and a list of document strings. First, count how many documents contain the target word at least once to determine the document frequency. Calculate the inverse document frequency by taking the natural logarithm of the total number of documents divided by the document frequency. For each document, count the occurrences of the target word and divide by the total number of words in that document to get the term frequency. Multiply the term frequency by the inverse document frequency for each document. Return a list of the resulting float scores. For example, targeting "apple" in ["apple pie", "banana"] returns [0.34, 0.0].

title: Ray Tracer Intersection
spec: Determine if and where a three dimensional light ray hits a sphere. The function `intersect(scene)` takes a tuple containing the ray origin, the ray direction, the sphere center, and the sphere radius. Subtract the sphere center from the ray origin to find the offset vector. Calculate the quadratic coefficients by taking the dot product of the direction with itself, twice the dot product of the offset and direction, and the dot product of the offset with itself minus the squared radius. Compute the discriminant to check if roots exist. If the discriminant is non negative, find the smallest positive root which represents the distance along the ray. Return the intersection distance, or negative one if there is no hit. For example, providing ((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), (0, 0, 5), 1.0) returns 4.0.

title: Checksum Padding Algorithm
spec: Calculate the parity bits for a digital message using a cyclic redundancy check approach. The function `checksum(bits)` receives a string of ones and zeros representing the message. Append eight zero bits to the end of the message to make room for the remainder. Define a generator polynomial string of length nine, such as one zero zero one one zero zero zero one. Iterate through the padded message bit by bit. Whenever the current leading bit is a one, perform a bitwise exclusive or between the next nine bits of the message and the polynomial. If the leading bit is a zero, do nothing and move to the next position. After processing all original message bits, extract the last eight bits as the final checksum and return them.

title: Color Space Converter
spec: Convert a color represented by hue, saturation, and lightness into standard red, green, and blue components. The function `convert(color)` receives a tuple of three floats where the first is an angle up to three hundred sixty and the others are percentages up to one. First, calculate the chroma by multiplying the saturation by one minus the absolute value of twice the lightness minus one. Find the intermediate value by multiplying the chroma by one minus the absolute value of the hue divided by sixty modulo two minus one. Assign these values to the red, green, and blue channels based on which sixty degree sector the hue falls into. Finally, add the lightness minus half the chroma to each channel, multiply by two hundred fifty five, and return a tuple of rounded integers. For example, providing (120.0, 1.0, 0.5) returns (0, 255, 0).

title: Audio Waveform Resampler
spec: Change the sample rate of a digital audio signal using linear interpolation. The function `resample(signal)` takes a tuple of an original sample list, the original sample rate, and the target sample rate. Calculate the ratio of the original rate to the target rate to determine the step size. For each index in the new signal, multiply the index by the step size to find the exact fractional position in the original signal. Separate this position into an integer base index and a fractional remainder. Interpolate between the value at the base index and the next index by weighting them according to the remainder. Return a list of the newly calculated samples. For example, providing ([0, 10, 20], 2, 3) returns a list of four resampled points.

title: Dice Game Evaluator
spec: Determine the maximum possible score for a roll of five six sided dice across several standard categories. The function `evaluate(dice)` takes a list of five integers. Count the frequency of each die face to identify multiples. If there are three of one number and two of another, calculate the sum for a full house score. Check for a sequence of four or five consecutive numbers to award a small or large straight score respectively. If all five dice show the same number, award fifty points for a maximum match. Sum all the dice for the chance category. Return the highest score among all applicable categories. For example, providing [2, 2, 2, 3, 3] returns 25 for a full house.

title: Polygon Area Calculator
spec: Calculate the internal area of a two dimensional closed polygon given its vertices. The function `area(vertices)` accepts a list of tuples, each containing an horizontal and vertical coordinate. Ensure the polygon is closed by implicitly connecting the last vertex back to the first vertex. Iterate through the edges of the polygon, taking pairs of adjacent vertices. For each pair, multiply the first horizontal coordinate by the second vertical coordinate, and subtract the product of the first vertical coordinate and the second horizontal coordinate. Accumulate these differences into a running total. Divide the absolute value of the final total by two to obtain the enclosed area. Return the resulting float. For example, providing [(0, 0), (0, 4), (3, 0)] returns 6.0.

title: Network Address Expander
spec: Expand a compressed Internet Protocol version six address into its full canonical representation. The function `expand(address)` receives a string representing the shortened address. Split the address by the double colon to separate the left and right portions. Count the number of colon separated segments in both portions to determine how many zero segments are missing from the total of eight. Create a list of zero segments to fill the gap. Recombine the left portion, the zero segments, and the right portion into a single list of eight segments. Pad each segment with leading zeros until it is exactly four characters long. Return the fully expanded string joined by colons. For example, providing "2001:db8::1" returns "2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001".

title: Scheduled Task Parser
spec: Parse a standard time scheduling string into a list of specific execution minutes. The function `parse(expression)` takes a string representing the minute field of a schedule. If the field is a single asterisk, generate all minutes from zero to fifty nine. If the field contains a slash, split it to find the step value and generate minutes starting from zero and jumping by the step. If it contains a hyphen, extract the start and end bounds and generate all integers in that inclusive range. If it is a simple number, parse it and return a list containing just that number. Return the sorted list of matching minutes. For example, providing "*/15" returns [0, 15, 30, 45].

title: Day of Week Calculator
spec: Determine the day of the week for any given date using mental math shortcuts. The function `doomsday(date)` receives a tuple of the year, month, and day. Extract the century and the last two digits of the year. Calculate the anchor day for the century by finding the remainder of the century divided by four, multiplying by five, and adding a constant. Determine the year anchor by adding the year digits, their integer division by four, and the century anchor. Find the specific doomsday for the given month, such as the last day of February or the fourth of April. Calculate the difference between the given day and the month doomsday, add it to the year anchor, and find the remainder modulo seven to get the final day index. For example, providing (2023, 10, 31) returns 2.

title: Continued Fraction Generator
spec: Convert a floating point number into a sequence of continued fraction terms. The function `fraction(number)` takes a single float as input. Extract the integer part of the number by truncating it, and append this to the results list. Subtract the integer part from the number to find the fractional remainder. If the remainder is extremely close to zero, terminate the process to avoid precision issues. Otherwise, take the reciprocal of the remainder to form the next intermediate value. Repeat the extraction of the integer part and the reciprocal of the remainder for up to ten iterations. Return the list of integer terms. For example, providing 3.245 returns a list of integers starting with 3.

title: Matrix Column Mixer
spec: Perform a simplified column mixing operation similar to modern block ciphers. The function `mix(column)` takes a list of four integers. Multiply each integer by a predefined polynomial in a Galois field of two hundred fifty six. For a multiplication by two, shift the bits to the left by one, and if the original number exceeded one hundred twenty seven, bitwise exclusive or the result with twenty seven. For a multiplication by three, exclusive or the multiplication by two with the original number. Combine the four transformed integers using exclusive or operations according to a specific mixing matrix. Return the new list of four integers. For example, providing [212, 212, 212, 213] returns a mixed column list.

title: Navigation Sentence Parser
spec: Extract location and speed data from a standard maritime navigation sentence. The function `parse(sentence)` receives a string starting with a dollar sign. Verify the integrity of the data by calculating the bitwise exclusive or of all characters between the dollar sign and the asterisk, and compare it to the hexadecimal checksum provided at the end. Split the payload by commas to isolate the individual fields. Extract the latitude and longitude, converting them from degrees and decimal minutes into pure decimal degrees, negating them if the hemisphere is south or west. Extract the speed in knots and multiply by one point eight five two to get kilometers per hour. Return a tuple of latitude, longitude, and speed. For example, a valid sentence string returns (48.1173, 11.5166, 41.48).

title: Hardware Address Formatter
spec: Clean and analyze a network interface hardware address. The function `normalize(address)` takes a string that may contain hyphens, colons, or dots. Strip all punctuation from the string and convert the remaining hexadecimal characters to uppercase. Verify that the resulting string has exactly twelve characters. Insert a colon after every second character to create a standard presentation format. Extract the first two characters, treat them as a hexadecimal integer, and verify the second least significant bit for local administration and the least significant bit for multicast. Return a tuple containing the standardized string, a boolean indicating if it is local, and a boolean indicating if it is multicast. For example, providing "00-1B-44-11-3A-B7" returns ("00:1B:44:11:3A:B7", false, false).

title: One Dimensional Clustering
spec: Group a list of numeric values into two distinct clusters based on their proximity to moving centroids. The function `cluster(data)` takes a list of numbers. Initialize the two centroids by finding the minimum and maximum values in the data. Create a loop that will run until the assignments of data points to clusters stop changing. Inside the loop, clear the two cluster lists. For each number in the data, calculate its absolute distance to both centroids and assign it to the cluster with the smaller distance. After all points are assigned, recalculate each centroid by finding the arithmetic mean of its assigned points. Return a tuple containing the two lists of clustered numbers. For example, providing [1.0, 2.0, 8.0, 9.0] returns ([1.0, 2.0], [8.0, 9.0]).

title: Sliding Window Decompressor
spec: Decompress a stream of data encoded with a sliding window algorithm. The function `decompress(stream)` receives a list of tuples, where each tuple represents either a literal character or a back reference. If the tuple contains a single element, treat it as a literal character and append it to the output buffer. If the tuple contains two integers, they represent a distance backwards and a length. Calculate the starting position by subtracting the distance from the current length of the output buffer. Iterate exactly length times, copying characters from the starting position to the end of the buffer, allowing for overlaps where the copied data extends into the newly appended data. Return the final decompressed string. For example, providing [("A",), (1, 3)] returns "AAAA".

title: Tennis Match Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(points)` that takes a string of points won by two players and returns the final set score. The characters denote which player won a point, using the letters a and b. The logic must track games, sets, and tiebreakers according to standard tennis rules. A game is won by reaching four points with a margin of two, except at six games all where a tiebreak is played to seven points with a two-point margin. The function returns a tuple of the final game counts for each player. For example, a sequence of twenty-four consecutive points for the first player returns six and zero.

title: Ballistic Trajectory Simulator
spec: Create a function `simulate(parameters)` that calculates the flight path of a projectile. The input tuple provides initial velocity, launch angle in degrees, height, mass, and a drag coefficient. The simulation must update the position iteratively using small time increments until the object hits the ground. It should account for gravity acting downwards and drag forces opposing the current velocity vector. Return a tuple containing the maximum height reached and the total horizontal distance traveled. Example: throwing at forty five degrees from the ground with no drag should yield the standard parabolic range.

title: Mortgage Amortization Generator
spec: Implement a function `amortize(loan)` that takes a principal amount, annual interest rate, and duration in months. It must compute the fixed monthly payment required to fully pay off the loan. Then, it needs to simulate each month, calculating how much of the payment goes to interest versus principal, and track the remaining balance. The function returns a list of tuples for each year showing the total interest paid and principal paid in that year. A small final payment adjustment might be necessary to bring the balance exactly to zero.

title: Custom Markup Stripper
spec: Develop `clean(text)` to process a custom document format and return plain text. The input text contains formatting tags enclosed in curly braces, block quotes starting with a greater than sign, and lists starting with asterisks. The logic must strip all formatting tags, properly collapse block quotes into single lines, and convert asterisk lists into numbered lists starting at one. Any nested tags must be handled from the inside out, and consecutive blank lines must be reduced to a single blank line. Example: an input with a bold tag and a two item list should return the text without braces and numbered one and two.

title: Playfair Cipher Decoder
spec: Write a function `decipher(payload)` where the input is a tuple of a ciphertext string and a keyword. The logic must first construct a five by five alphabet grid from the keyword, omitting the letter j. Then it divides the message into pairs of letters and applies the decryption rules: if the letters share a row or column, shift them accordingly, and if they form a rectangle, swap their columns. It should return the fully decrypted string in lowercase. Example: decrypting with the keyword secret and a valid ciphertext returns the original plaintext message.

title: Moving Average Crossover Backtester
spec: Implement a function `backtest(prices)` that simulates a trading strategy over a sequence of daily stock prices. The logic must calculate a short term moving average over five days and a long term moving average over twenty days. When the short average crosses above the long average, it simulates buying one share, and when it crosses below, it simulates selling. The function must track the cash balance and the current holdings, starting with zero cash and zero shares. It returns the final portfolio value assuming all remaining shares are liquidated at the final day's price.

title: Project Critical Path
spec: Design `evaluate(tasks)` to compute the earliest possible completion time for a project. The input is a list of tuples containing a task identifier, its duration in days, and a list of prerequisite task identifiers. The logic must first identify tasks with no prerequisites and set their start times to zero. It must then iteratively find tasks whose prerequisites have all been scheduled, setting their start times based on the maximum completion time of those prerequisites. The function returns the overall completion time of the entire project.

title: Genetic Mutation Tracker
spec: Create a function `analyze(sequences)` that takes a reference genetic sequence and a mutated sequence. The logic must transcribe both sequences into codons, which are groups of three letters, and map them to standard amino acids. It should identify whether the mutations cause a silent change, where the amino acid remains the same, or a missense change, where the amino acid differs. The function returns a list of tuples describing the position of the altered codon, the original amino acid, and the new amino acid. If a stop codon is introduced prematurely, the sequence parsing must halt immediately.

title: First Fit Bin Packer
spec: Write a function `pack(items)` to simulate packing a list of item weights into containers of a fixed capacity of ten. The logic must iterate through each item weight and attempt to place it into the earliest available container that has enough remaining space. If no existing container can hold the item, a new container must be opened. The function needs to return a list of lists, where each inner list represents the items stored in a specific container. For example, placing three items weighing four, five, and six should result in two containers being used.

title: Web Session Duration Analyzer
spec: Implement `sessions(logs)` to calculate user engagement times from a list of web server log entries. Each entry is a tuple containing a user identifier, a timestamp in seconds, and an action type. The logic must group all events by the user identifier and sort them chronologically. A session is considered ended if a user is inactive for more than thirty minutes, which should split their events into multiple distinct sessions. The function returns a list of session durations in seconds across all users, ignoring sessions that consist of only a single event.

title: Reversi Valid Move Finder
spec: Create a function `evaluate(board)` that takes an eight by eight grid representing a Reversi game state and determines all valid placements for the current player. The current player is represented by a one, the opponent by a two, and empty spaces by zero. The logic must scan the board for every empty space and check all eight directions for a continuous line of opponent pieces terminating in a piece owned by the current player. The function returns a list of tuples representing the row and column coordinates where the current player can legally place a piece.

title: Distance Vector Router
spec: Write a function `route(links)` that computes the shortest path routing table for a small computer network. The input is a list of connections, each containing two node identifiers and a positive integer representing the link cost. The logic should start by initializing distance tables for all unique nodes, setting the distance to themselves as zero and all others as infinite. It must then repeatedly relax the distances by sharing routing tables between directly connected neighbors until no further changes occur. The function returns a list of tuples containing the starting node, destination node, and the minimum cost.

title: Syllable Hyphenation Engine
spec: Implement `hyphenate(word)` to insert hyphens into an English word based on basic phonotactic rules. The logic must identify vowels and consonants, handling the letter y as a vowel if it contains no other vowels. It should split words between double consonants and between two consonants bounded by vowels, while keeping common consonant digraphs like sh and ch together. A silent e at the end of the word must not be treated as a separate syllable. The function returns the word as a string with hyphens inserted at the appropriate syllable boundaries.

title: Ascii Histogram Generator
spec: Develop `visualize(data)` to create a text based histogram from a list of floating point numbers. The logic must first determine the minimum and maximum values in the dataset to establish the overall range, padding the maximum slightly so the largest value fits in the final bin. It should divide the range into exactly ten equal sized bins and count the number of data points that fall into each bin. The function returns a list of strings, where each string represents a bin with a row of hash characters corresponding to its count, scaled so the largest bin is exactly twenty characters wide.

title: Convex Hull Finder
spec: Write `enclose(points)` to compute the convex hull for a set of two dimensional coordinates. The input is a list of tuples representing x and y values. The logic must find the point with the lowest y coordinate to use as the pivot, then sort all other points by the polar angle they make with the pivot. It should iterate through the sorted points, maintaining a sequence of hull vertices and discarding any point that creates a clockwise turn. The function returns the list of points that form the outer boundary of the set in counterclockwise order.

title: Signal Noise Smoother
spec: Implement a function `smooth(signal)` that applies a sliding window median filter to a sequence of sensor readings. The input is a list of numerical values representing a sampled signal. The logic must slide a window of size five across the sequence, extracting the local neighborhood for each point. Near the edges where a full window is not available, the window should shrink to include only the available neighboring points. For each window, the values must be sorted to find the median, which then replaces the original value in the output sequence. Return the new filtered list.

title: Coordinate K-Means Clustering
spec: Create `cluster(points)` to divide a list of two dimensional coordinates into three distinct groups. The logic must randomly select three initial center points from the input data. In a loop, it should assign every point to the closest center using Euclidean distance, then recalculate the three centers by finding the average coordinates of all points in each group. This assignment and update process repeats until the centers no longer move between iterations. The function returns a list of three lists, each containing the coordinates assigned to one of the final clusters.

title: Directory Tree Size Rollup
spec: Write `rollup(files)` to calculate the total size of all directories in a simulated file system. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a file path string separated by slashes and an integer file size. The logic must parse each path, separating the directory components from the file name. It should aggregate the sizes, ensuring that a file's size is added not only to its immediate parent directory but also propagated up to all ancestor directories including the root. The function returns a list of tuples pairing each unique directory path with its total accumulated size.

title: Business Hours Calculator
spec: Implement `calculate(intervals)` to determine the total billable hours from a list of work shift start and end times. The input consists of tuples with start and end timestamps in minutes since midnight. The logic must filter out any time worked before nine in the morning or after five in the afternoon, as those are outside standard business hours. It must also handle overlapping shifts by merging them into continuous blocks of time before calculating the duration. The function returns the total valid working time in hours, rounded down to the nearest integer.

title: Nonogram Row Validator
spec: Develop `validate(puzzle)` to check if a sequence of filled and empty squares satisfies a set of numeric clues. The input is a tuple containing a list of integers representing the clues and a string of hashes and dots representing filled and empty cells. The logic must count the lengths of consecutive filled segments in the string, completely ignoring the empty cells between them. It then compares this sequence of lengths against the provided clues to ensure they match exactly in size and order. The function returns true if the row is perfectly valid according to the rules, and false otherwise.

title: URL Query Parameter Parser
spec: Write `parse(url)` to extract and decode query parameters from a web address string. The logic must first split the string at the question mark to isolate the query portion from the main address. It should then divide the query by ampersands to separate individual key and value pairs. Any percent encoded characters in the keys or values must be converted back to their standard character representations, and plus signs should be replaced with spaces. The function returns a list of tuples containing the decoded keys and values, ignoring any pairs that lack an equals sign.

title: Network Page Ranker
spec: Create `rank(graph)` to compute the importance scores of web pages in a tiny network. The input is a list of directed links between pages, represented as pairs of node identifiers. The logic should initialize all pages with an equal score summing to one. In each iteration, every page distributes its current score equally among all its outgoing links, with a small damping factor applied to simulate random browsing. Pages with no outgoing links should distribute their score evenly across the entire network. The function runs for twenty iterations and returns the final scores as a list of tuples sorted from highest to lowest.

title: Intersection Traffic Simulator
spec: Implement `simulate(cars)` to model vehicle throughput at a traffic light. The input is a list of integers representing the arrival times of vehicles in seconds. The logic must maintain a timer and a queue of waiting vehicles. The traffic light operates on a fixed cycle: green for thirty seconds, then red for thirty seconds. During a green phase, one vehicle can pass through the intersection every two seconds. The function must track the delay experienced by each vehicle, calculated as the difference between its arrival time and the time it passes the light, and return the maximum delay observed.

title: Lunar Phase Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(days)` that approximates the moon phase based on the number of days elapsed since a known new moon. The logic must divide the days by the standard lunar cycle length of roughly twenty nine point five days to find the current position in the cycle. It should then map this fractional progress to one of four primary phases: new moon, first quarter, full moon, or last quarter. A tolerance window of two days should be used around the exact quarter points to categorize the phase. Return the name of the phase as a simple string.

title: Molecular Mass Calculator
spec: Develop `calculate(formula)` to compute the total atomic mass of a chemical compound from its string representation. The formula consists of element symbols, which start with an uppercase letter followed optionally by a lowercase letter, and numerical quantities. The logic must parse the string character by character to group element names and their associated numbers. If an element has no explicit number following it, the quantity is assumed to be one. It should look up the atomic mass for each element using a predefined mapping for common elements like carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, and return the total mass as a float.

title: Baking Recipe Scaler
spec: Write the entry point `scale(recipe)` which takes a tuple containing original servings, target servings, and a list of tuples representing ingredients. Each ingredient tuple holds the name, amount, and measurement unit. First find the scaling factor by dividing the target by the original servings. For each ingredient multiply the amount by the factor. If the new amount in cups is less than one quarter, convert it to tablespoons. If tablespoons are less than one, convert to teaspoons. Round all final amounts to two decimal places. Return a list of tuples with the updated amount and unit for each ingredient name.

title: Mayan Calendar Converter
spec: Implement `convert(days)` to translate an integer number of days passed since the epoch into the historical long count format. First divide the total days by one hundred forty four thousand to find the baktun cycle. Find the remainder and divide by seven thousand two hundred for the katun cycle. Next divide the remaining days by three hundred sixty for the tun, then by twenty for the winal, leaving the remaining days as the kin. Return a tuple of five integers representing these five periods in strictly descending order of duration.

title: Text Readability Scorer
spec: Create `evaluate(text)` to compute reading grade levels from a plain string of prose. Split the text into sentences using periods, exclamation marks, and question marks as delimiters. Count the total number of words by splitting on spaces and removing empty strings. Count the total syllables by finding contiguous groups of vowels, subtracting one for every silent trailing e at the end of a word. Calculate the average words per sentence and average syllables per word. Combine these using the standard reading ease formula to determine a school grade level. Return the rounded integer grade.

title: Bank Loan Risk Assessor
spec: Write `assess(applicant)` where the input is a tuple containing applicant age, credit score, monthly income, requested loan amount, and months of employment. Calculate the debt to income ratio by dividing the requested amount by the monthly income multiplied by twelve. If the credit score is below six hundred, automatically reject the application. If the age is under eighteen or employment is less than six months, add a high risk penalty deduction. Assign a final score out of one hundred by starting with the credit score mapped to a percentage, deducting points for high ratios and penalties. Return a string stating either approved or rejected, alongside the final score.

title: Escape Room Lock Simulator
spec: Provide the function `unlock(moves)` taking a list of integers representing rotational clicks on a puzzle with four interlocking rings. Each ring starts at zero and goes up to nine. A positive integer rotates the first ring forward, but every full revolution of the first ring pulls the second ring forward by one notch. A negative integer rotates the third ring backward, pulling the fourth ring if passing zero. Process the sequence of movements step by step, applying modulo arithmetic to keep positions between zero and nine. Return a tuple of four integers representing the final positions of the rings.

title: Crop Rotation Planner
spec: Implement `plan(history)` taking a list of strings representing the plant families grown in a single field over previous seasons. Check the most recent crop. If it was a legume, the soil has excess nitrogen, so the next recommendation must be a heavy feeder like a nightshade. If the last two were nightshades, a disease break is required, so recommend a grass. If the field was left fallow, recommend a root vegetable to loosen the soil. Default to legumes if no other rule triggers or the history is empty. Return the string name of the recommended plant family.

title: Freight Train Loader
spec: Create `load(freight)` which takes a list of integers representing shipping container weights. The train consists of cars that can each hold up to one hundred thousand pounds. Start placing containers into the first car in the exact order they arrive. If a container causes the current car to exceed its limit, close the current car and start a new empty one. If a single container exceeds the maximum capacity of an empty car, ignore it completely and skip to the next container in line. Return a list of lists, where each inner list contains the weights assigned to one specific car.

title: Water Bill Calculator
spec: Write `bill(usage)` where the input is a tuple of an integer representing gallons consumed and a boolean indicating if the customer is low income. Start with a flat service charge of fifteen dollars. The first five thousand gallons cost two dollars per thousand. The next five thousand cost three dollars and fifty cents per thousand. Any usage beyond ten thousand gallons costs five dollars per thousand. Add a drought surcharge of ten percent to the total usage costs, excluding the flat service charge. If the low income flag is true, subtract a flat five dollar credit from the final total. Return the total bill rounded to two decimal places.

title: Fantasy Combat Simulator
spec: Provide `clash(fighters)` taking a tuple of two combatants, where each combatant is a tuple of health, attack power, defense, and an elemental type string. For up to ten rounds, the first fighter attacks the second, and then the second attacks the first. Calculate base damage as attack minus defense, with a minimum of one. Double the damage if the attacker element beats the defender element, such as water beating fire. Subtract the damage from the defender health. If either health drops to zero or below, stop the fight early. Return the remaining health of both fighters as a tuple.

title: Flight Waypoint Router
spec: Implement `route(waypoints)` which receives a list of tuples containing latitude, longitude, and altitude for a flight path. Calculate the straight line distance between consecutive points using a standard geometric formula. If the altitude increases between points, multiply the distance segment by a climb factor of one point two to account for extra fuel usage. If the altitude decreases, multiply by a descent factor of point eight. Accumulate all the adjusted distance segments across the entire journey. Return the total adjusted flight distance rounded to the nearest integer.

title: Optical Character Corrector
spec: Create `correct(scan)` taking a raw string of text from a scanned document. Step through each character. If a numeric zero is surrounded by alphabetical letters, change it to an uppercase oh. If an exclamation mark appears inside a word, change it to a lowercase ell. Remove any extra spaces that appear directly before punctuation marks like periods or commas. Finally, capitalize the first letter of any word that immediately follows a period and a space. Return the completely corrected string.

title: Traffic Light Sequencer
spec: Write `sequence(lanes)` which receives a tuple of four integers representing the number of waiting cars in the north, south, east, and west lanes. A single traffic cycle allocates green light time to the north-south axis and then the east-west axis. Each waiting car requires three seconds to pass. Determine the time needed for north and south to empty, taking the maximum of the two lane requirements. Cap this axis time at a maximum of sixty seconds. Repeat the identical logic for the east-west axis. Add five seconds of yellow light time after each axis phase. Return the total cycle length in seconds.

title: Dietary Restriction Filter
spec: Implement `filter(menu)` where the input is a list of tuples, each containing a dish name, a calorie count, and a string of comma separated ingredients. The user is allergic to peanuts and shellfish, and wants to eat vegetarian. Iterate through the menu dishes. Reject any dish that contains peanuts, shrimp, crab, or chicken in its ingredients string. Reject any dish that exceeds eight hundred calories. For the remaining valid dishes, strip leading and trailing whitespace from the dish names and format them in all uppercase. Return a list of the approved dish names.

title: Ski Resort Snowmaker
spec: Create `snow(conditions)` taking a tuple of ambient temperature, relative humidity, and target base depth. First calculate the wet bulb temperature using a standard approximation formula subtracting a fraction of the humidity from the ambient temperature. If the wet bulb is above freezing, return zero since artificial snow cannot be made. If it is below freezing, calculate the production rate which increases linearly the colder and drier the air gets. Divide the target base depth by the production rate to find the required running time. Return the hours rounded up to the nearest whole integer.

title: Transit Fare Calculator
spec: Provide `fare(trips)` where the input is a list of integers representing transit zones traveled for each trip in a month. A trip entirely within one zone costs two dollars and fifty cents. A trip crossing into a second zone costs three dollars. A trip across three or more zones costs four dollars. Sum up the cost of all individual trips by iterating through the travel log. If the total cumulative cost exceeds a monthly unlimited pass price of ninety dollars, cap the cost at ninety dollars. Return the final monetary amount the rider owes.

title: Beehive Population Model
spec: Implement `simulate(colony)` taking a tuple of initial adult population and a list of daily average temperatures. Track a queue of eggs maturing over time. On each day, if the temperature is above fifty degrees, bees forage and gather food, allowing the queen to lay one hundred new eggs. If the temperature falls below fifty, no food is gathered and ten adult bees die from the cold. Eggs take exactly three days to mature into adult bees, meaning eggs laid on day one are added to the adult total on day four. Return the final adult bee population after all days are processed.

title: Obfuscated Morse Decoder
spec: Write `decode(signals)` receiving a list of integers. Positive integers represent the duration of an audible beep, negative integers represent the duration of silence. A beep duration of one or two is classified as a dot, while three or four is a dash. A silence of one or two separates parts of a single letter. A silence of three or four separates distinct letters, and a silence of five or more separates entire words. Map the assembled sequences of dots and dashes to standard english letters. Return the fully decoded sentence as a plain string.

title: Warehouse Robot Pathfinder
spec: Create `navigate(grid)` where the input is a list of strings representing a two dimensional warehouse map. Empty spaces are periods, obstacles are hashes, and items to pick up are asterisks. The robot starts at the top left corner facing east. Move the robot forward one step at a time until it hits an obstacle or the wall, at which point it must turn right. If it gets stuck in a corner unable to move forward or right, turn left instead. Every time the robot lands on an asterisk, increment a collection counter and change that spot to a period. Stop the simulation after exactly one hundred moves and return the total number of items collected.

title: Medieval Jousting Tournament
spec: Implement `tournament(knights)` which takes a list of tuples. Each tuple has a knight name, their horsemanship skill, and their lance strength. Pair the knights up sequentially for the first round. In each match, calculate a score by multiplying horsemanship by two and adding the lance strength. The knight with the higher score wins and moves to the next round, but their lance strength is reduced by one due to wear and tear from the bout. Continue pairing the remaining winners until only one knight remains undefeated. Return the string name of the overall champion.

title: Plant Watering Schedule
spec: Provide `schedule(plants)` receiving a list of tuples detailing plant name, days since last watered, and a drought tolerance string. If tolerance is low, it must be watered every three days. If medium, every seven days. If high, every fourteen days. Calculate how many days are left until each plant needs water by subtracting the days since last watered from the required frequency. If the days left is negative, set it to zero to indicate it needs water immediately. Group the plants by the number of days left. Return a list of plant names that need watering on day zero.

title: Hash Avalanche Tester
spec: Write `avalanche(blocks)` taking a tuple of two byte strings of equal length representing a cryptographic hash input and output. First check that they are exactly sixteen bytes long, throwing an error otherwise. Convert both byte sequences to binary strings. Iterate through the individual bits to count how many bits differ between the first block and the second block, which represents the hamming distance. Calculate the percentage of bits that changed relative to the total number of bits. Return true if the percentage is strictly greater than forty five percent and less than fifty five percent.

title: Vending Machine Restocking
spec: Create `restock(inventory)` taking a list of tuples containing slot number, item name, current quantity, and days until expiration. Iterate through each slot to evaluate its status. If the days until expiration is less than three, the item must be removed entirely, so treat the current quantity as zero. If the current quantity is below five, calculate how many items are needed to reach the maximum slot capacity of twelve. Accumulate the total cost of all needed replacement items, assuming a flat wholesale cost of fifty cents per unit. Return the total monetary restocking cost.

title: Wind Turbine Estimator
spec: Implement `estimate(wind)` receiving a list of integers representing wind speeds in meters per second over a twenty four hour period. For each hour, evaluate the speed. If it is below three or above twenty five, the turbine generates zero power due to cutoff limits. Between three and twelve, the power output is the speed cubed multiplied by ten. Between twelve and twenty five, the turbine operates at its maximum rated capacity of two thousand kilowatts. Sum the power generated across all twenty four hours. Return the total daily energy production as an integer.

title: Library Penalty Calculator
spec: Provide `penalize(returns)` where the input is a list of tuples, each having a patron type string and a days overdue integer. Iterate through the returned books. For a standard patron, the daily fee is twenty five cents. For a student, the daily fee is ten cents. If a standard patron is overdue by more than thirty days, add a flat twenty dollar replacement charge. Students never pay the replacement charge. Cap the maximum daily fee accumulation at ten dollars, before adding any applicable replacement charges. Sum and return the total fines collected for all returns.

title: Carpet Installation Estimator
spec: Write `quote(rooms)` taking a list of tuples, where each tuple contains room length, room width, and a boolean indicating if it has stairs. Calculate the area of each room in square feet by multiplying length by width. Multiply the total square footage of all rooms by a base carpet price of three dollars per square foot. If a room has stairs, add a flat labor surcharge of fifty dollars for that specific room. Add a ten percent waste margin to the final total cost to account for installation offcuts and edge trimming. Return the grand total rounded to two decimal places.

title: Ferry Passenger Ticketing
spec: Write a function `fare(passengers)` to calculate ferry crossing fees. The input is a list of tuples containing passenger age, vehicle length in feet, a boolean for pulling a trailer, and a boolean for resident status. The base fare is fifteen dollars per passenger. If the passenger is bringing a vehicle, add an extra two dollars per foot of vehicle length. If they are pulling a trailer, apply a flat fifty dollar surcharge to the vehicle fee. Passengers over the age of sixty get a five dollar discount on their base fare, while children under five travel for free. If the resident status is true, apply a thirty percent discount to the final calculated total. Keep track of the total revenue generated. Return a tuple containing a list of individual fares and the final total revenue.

title: Hospital Triage Queue
spec: Write a function `triage(patients)` to prioritize a hospital waitlist. The input is a list of tuples containing patient name, severity level from one to five where one is most severe, age, and arrival time in minutes since midnight. First, separate all patients with severity one; they always go first. For the remaining patients, calculate a priority score starting with their arrival time. Subtract thirty points from this score if the patient is under twelve or over seventy years old. Subtract an additional fifty points if their severity is level two. Sort the patients based on this calculated score from lowest to highest. If scores tie, the younger patient goes first. Return a list of patient names in the exact order they should be seen by the doctor.

title: Drone Flight Battery Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate(maneuvers)` to estimate the remaining battery life of a drone. The input is a list of tuples representing flight maneuvers, each containing an action string such as climb, hover, or cruise, and a duration in seconds. The drone starts with one hundred percent battery. Hovering drains zero point one percent per second. Climbing drains zero point three percent per second. Cruising drains zero point two percent per second. If a climb is immediately followed by a cruise, the cruise receives a bonus headwind efficiency, reducing its drain to zero point one five percent per second for that maneuver. If the battery drops to zero or below at any point, immediately halt processing and return zero. Otherwise, return the final battery percentage rounded to one decimal place.

title: Hotel Room Upgrade Logic
spec: Write a function `upgrade(guests, rooms)` to process hotel room upgrades. The first input is a list of guest tuples containing their name, loyalty tier integer from one to four where four is highest, and length of stay in nights. The second input is a list of available room tuples containing room type string, capacity, and current available count. Sort the guests by loyalty tier descending, then by shortest length of stay ascending. Iterate through the sorted guests and attempt to assign the best room available. Tier four guests should be assigned a suite if available, otherwise a deluxe room, otherwise a standard. Lower tiers only qualify for standard rooms. Subtract from the room availability as assignments are made. Return a list of tuples pairing the guest name with their assigned room type.

title: Coffee Shop Order Router
spec: Write a function `dispatch(orders)` to route coffee shop orders and estimate wait times. The input is a list of order tuples containing a category string such as espresso, blended, or food, a boolean for whether it is iced, and an integer representing the number of custom modifiers. Espresso orders take two minutes base time. Blended orders take four minutes. Food orders take three minutes. If any drink is iced, add one extra minute for preparation. Add thirty seconds for each custom modifier on any order. Keep a running total of the preparation time required for each of the three categories independently. Finally, return a tuple containing the total minutes required for the espresso station, the blended station, and the food station, all rounded up to the nearest whole minute.

title: Paint Mixing Ratio Calculator
spec: Write a function `mix(requests)` to calculate the ingredients needed for custom paint colors. The input is a list of tuples containing the desired color name, the total volume in gallons, and a boolean for gloss finish. The base required is the volume in gallons. If the color is crimson, it requires ten drops of red tint and two drops of blue tint per gallon. If the color is forest, it requires eight drops of green and four drops of blue per gallon. If the color is midnight, it requires twelve drops of blue and two drops of black per gallon. For a gloss finish, add half a gallon of gloss medium for every gallon of base volume. Keep a running tally of all base gallons, gloss gallons, and individual tint drops needed across all requests. Return a tuple containing total base, total gloss, total red drops, total green drops, total blue drops, and total black drops.

title: Subscription Billing Prorater
spec: Write a function `prorate(changes)` to calculate a prorated monthly subscription bill. The input is a list of tuples representing plan changes, each containing the day of the month the change occurred and the new monthly price. Assume a thirty day billing cycle. The subscription starts on day one at a cost of zero. For each change, determine how many days the previous plan was active before the change occurred. Multiply those active days by the daily rate of the previous plan, which is the monthly price divided by thirty. Sum these segments to find the total bill. The final plan remains active until the end of the thirtieth day. Return the total calculated cost for the month, rounded to two decimal places.
