title: Ski Rental Boot Fitter
spec: Write a function `fit(skiers)` to determine the optimal ski boot size and stiffness for customers. The input is a list of tuples containing the customer name, standard shoe size, and an ability integer from one to three representing beginner, intermediate, and expert. First, convert the standard shoe size to a base mondo size by adding eighteen. If the customer is a beginner, add one full size to the mondo size for comfort. If they are an expert, subtract half a size for performance and tighter control. Next, determine the flex rating. Beginners receive a flex of seventy, intermediates a flex of ninety, and experts a flex of one hundred and twenty. Return a list of tuples containing the customer name, their adjusted mondo size, and their assigned flex rating.

title: Pet Boarding Kennel Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(pets)` to assign boarding kennels to pets. The input is a list of tuples containing pet name, family identifier, size string being small or large, and a boolean for medical needs. Medical pets must always be assigned to solitary observation kennels, regardless of size or family. For the remaining pets, group them by their family identifier. Two small pets from the same family can share a single standard kennel. A large pet must always have its own large run, even if it has siblings. Any leftover small pets from a family get their own standard kennel. Count the total number of observation kennels, standard kennels, and large runs needed to accommodate all the pets. Return a tuple of these three integer counts.

title: Golf Handicap Calculator
spec: Write a function `handicap(rounds)` to calculate a golf handicap index. The input is a list of tuples representing rounds played, containing the gross score, the course rating, and the course slope. For each round, calculate the differential by subtracting the course rating from the gross score, multiplying the result by one hundred and thirteen, and dividing by the course slope. Round each differential to one decimal place. Sort the list of differentials from lowest to highest. If there are fewer than five rounds, return zero. If there are between five and ten rounds, average the lowest two differentials. If there are more than ten rounds, average the lowest eight. Multiply the final average by zero point nine six and return the result truncated to one decimal place.

title: Car Wash Queue Pricing
spec: Write a function `quote(vehicles)` to generate price quotes for a car wash. The input is a list of tuples containing the vehicle class string like sedan or truck, a boolean for heavy mud, and a boolean for premium wax. The base wash price is ten dollars for a sedan and fifteen dollars for a truck. If the heavy mud flag is true, add a five dollar prep fee. If the premium wax flag is true, add eight dollars to the price. Keep track of how many vehicles are being washed. If the customer is bringing in three or more vehicles at once, apply a ten percent discount to the entire total. Return a tuple containing the final total price rounded to two decimals and the count of vehicles processed.

title: Car Rental Fee Aggregator
spec: Write a function `invoice(rentals)` to generate car rental invoices. The input is a list of tuples containing the car size string like compact or suv, days rented, miles driven, and a boolean for prepaying fuel. The base daily rate is thirty dollars for a compact and fifty dollars for an suv. Renters are given one hundred free miles per day. Any miles driven over this allowance are billed at twenty five cents per mile. If the prepaid fuel flag is true, add a flat forty dollar fee to the total; otherwise, if the miles driven are over fifty, assume the tank needs filling and add a seventy dollar penalty. Sum all charges for each rental. Return a list of final totals rounded to two decimal places.

title: Archery Tournament Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(arrows)` to score a round of archery. The input is a list of tuples representing arrow shots, containing the ring hit integer from one to ten and the exact distance from the target center in millimeters. Hitting the outer rings from one to nine awards that exact face value in points. Hitting the ten ring awards ten points. However, if the distance from the center is less than two millimeters, the shot is a perfect bullseye and awards an extra two bonus points. If the ring hit is zero, it is a miss and deducts one point from the total score. If a player misses three consecutive times, apply an additional five point penalty. Return the final accumulated score.

title: Bicycle Gear Ratio Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(drivetrain)` to analyze bicycle gearing. The input is a tuple containing a list of front chainring tooth counts, a list of rear cog tooth counts, and the wheel circumference in millimeters. Iterate through every possible combination of front chainring and rear cog. Calculate the gear ratio by dividing the front teeth by the rear teeth. Multiply this ratio by the wheel circumference to find the development distance in millimeters. Exclude extreme cross chaining combinations, specifically the smallest front ring paired with the smallest rear cog, and the largest front ring paired with the largest rear cog. Sort the remaining valid development distances from lowest to highest. Return a list of these valid distances rounded to the nearest whole millimeter.

title: Theme Park Fast Pass Allocator
spec: Write a function `distribute(requests)` to allocate skip the line passes for a theme park. The input is a list of tuples containing the ride name, party size, and a boolean for VIP status. VIP requests are processed first, in the order they appear. Then, process the remaining regular requests. Each ride has a maximum capacity of ten fast passes per hour. Assign a starting time slot beginning at nine in the morning. Once a ride reaches its ten person capacity for that hour, advance its availability to the next hour. If a single party is larger than ten people, they must be split across multiple consecutive hours. Return a list of tuples pairing the ride name with the assigned time slot hour in military time format for each request.

title: Recycling Center Sorting Payout
spec: Write a function `payout(materials)` to calculate payments for recycled materials. The input is a list of tuples containing the material type string, the weight in pounds, and the contamination percentage. Aluminum pays fifty cents per pound, plastic pays twenty cents, and glass pays ten cents. If the contamination percentage is over twenty percent, the batch is rejected and pays zero. If the contamination is between ten and twenty percent, deduct thirty percent from the batch payout. If an aluminum batch weighs more than one hundred pounds and has less than five percent contamination, add a twenty dollar bulk bonus to its payout. Sum the total payments for all valid batches. Return the final amount rounded to two decimals.

title: Blood Bank Donor Eligibility
spec: Write a function `screen(donors)` to evaluate potential blood donors. The input is a list of tuples containing the donor name, age, weight in pounds, and days since their last donation. To be eligible, a donor must be at least seventeen years old and weigh at least one hundred and ten pounds. Standard donors must wait a minimum of fifty six days between donations. However, if the donor is over the age of sixty five, they must wait a minimum of eighty days between donations to ensure proper recovery. If a donor meets all these criteria, they are considered eligible. Compile a list of the eligible donors. Return this list of names in alphabetical order.

title: Bookkeeping Ledger Reconciler
spec: Write a function `reconcile(entries)` to balance an accounting ledger. The input is a list of tuples containing a transaction identifier, a category string which is either credit or debit, and a monetary amount. Separate the entries into a list of credits and a list of debits. Attempt to pair each credit with a debit of the exact same amount. If an exact match is found, remove both from their respective lists. For the remaining entries, attempt to find a match where the credit and debit amounts are within five cents of each other to account for rounding errors. Any entries still unmatched after this second pass are flagged as discrepancies. Return a list containing the transaction identifiers of all unmatched entries.

title: Pizza Delivery Route Bundler
spec: Write a function `bundle(orders)` to group pizza deliveries into efficient trips. The input is a list of tuples containing an address identifier, the distance from the store in miles, the number of pizzas, and a boolean for priority status. A delivery driver can carry a maximum of five pizzas per trip. Priority orders must always be assigned to a trip first before non priority orders. Group the orders to maximize the number of pizzas per trip without exceeding the five pizza limit. When grouping, prefer orders that are within two miles of each other to keep the driver in the same neighborhood. Return a list of trips, where each trip is a list of address identifiers representing the delivery sequence.

title: Baking Competition Scorer
spec: Write a function `judge(bakes)` to evaluate scores in a baking contest. The input is a list of tuples containing the contestant name, a taste score out of ten, a presentation score out of ten, and the number of minutes they went over the time limit. Taste is the most important metric, so multiply the taste score by two. Add the presentation score to the modified taste score to get the base total. Subtract one point from the total for every minute the contestant went over time. If a contestant receives a perfect ten in presentation, award them three bonus points. Any contestant with a taste score below four is immediately disqualified and scores zero. Return the name of the contestant with the highest final score.

title: Solar Panel Layout Optimizer
spec: Write a function `optimize(roofs)` to calculate potential solar power generation. The input is a list of tuples containing roof width in feet, roof height in feet, and a percentage of the roof that is shaded. Assume a standard solar panel is five feet wide and three feet tall, and produces three hundred watts. Calculate the maximum number of panels that can fit on the roof by dividing the width by five and the height by three, rounding down to whole numbers, and multiplying them together. Reduce this panel count by the shading percentage, rounding down to the nearest whole panel. Multiply the final number of viable panels by three hundred to find the total wattage. Return a list of wattages for all roofs.

title: Moving Truck Packer
spec: Write a function `pack(furniture)` to load a moving truck based on dimensions and fragility. The input is a list of tuples containing an item identifier, volume in cubic feet, a boolean for whether it is fragile, and an integer for weight in pounds. The truck has a maximum capacity of one thousand cubic feet and five thousand pounds. Sort the items so that heavy and non fragile items are packed first to create a stable base. Iterate through the items and add them to the truck as long as both the weight and volume capacities are not exceeded. If a fragile item is added, it requires an extra ten cubic feet of space for padding materials. Return a list of the item identifiers successfully loaded into the truck.

title: Employee Bonus Allocator
spec: Write a function `bonus(employees)` to calculate annual profit sharing bonuses. The input is a list of tuples containing the employee name, their base salary, years of service, and a performance rating from one to five. The standard bonus is five percent of the base salary. If the performance rating is four or five, increase the bonus percentage to eight percent. If the rating is one or two, the bonus percentage drops to zero. For every full year of service over five years, add an extra five hundred dollars flat to their calculated bonus amount. Finally, cap the maximum possible bonus at ten thousand dollars to ensure fair distribution across the company. Return a list of tuples pairing the employee name with their final calculated bonus.

title: Produce Ripeness Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(produce)` to sort agricultural produce based on ripeness metrics. The input is a list of tuples containing the fruit type string, days since harvest, and a firmness score from one to ten. Bananas are ready if harvested between three and five days ago and have a firmness below six. Apples are ready if harvested over seven days ago and have a firmness above eight. Avocados are ready if harvested between five and eight days ago and have a firmness exactly equal to four. Any fruit that has been harvested for more than fourteen days is considered spoiled regardless of firmness. Return a tuple containing three lists: one for ready fruits, one for unripe fruits that need more time, and one for spoiled fruits.

title: Call Center Router
spec: Write a function `redirect(calls)` to route incoming customer service calls. The input is a list of tuples containing a caller identifier, the issue category string like billing or technical, and the wait time in minutes. There are three available agents: a billing specialist, a technical specialist, and a general support agent. Route billing issues to the billing specialist and technical issues to the technical specialist. However, if any caller has been waiting for more than fifteen minutes, their call is immediately routed to the general support agent to reduce wait times, regardless of the issue category. Keep a count of how many calls each agent receives. Return a tuple containing the call counts for the billing, technical, and general agents respectively.

title: Employee Paycheck Withholding
spec: `payroll(data)` takes a list of employee records where each record is a tuple of gross pay, dependents, and a boolean for management status. Calculate the net pay for each. Deduct social security at 6.2 percent up to a maximum gross of 140000. Deduct medicare at 1.45 percent on all gross pay, with an extra 0.9 percent for gross over 200000. For federal income tax, deduct 10 percent for the first 10000, 12 percent up to 40000, and 22 percent for any amount above. Reduce the taxable gross for federal tax by 2000 per dependent before applying the brackets. Management gets a flat bonus of 500 added to their net pay. Return a list of net pay amounts rounded to two decimals. For example, given [(50000, 2, False)], the calculations lead to a final net pay of 40255.0, so it returns [40255.0].

title: Airline Luggage Fee
spec: `baggage(passengers)` takes a list of passenger records containing loyalty status, base ticket price, and a list of bag weights in pounds. Calculate total baggage fees for each passenger. The first bag is 30 dollars, the second is 40 dollars, and additional bags are 100 dollars each. If a bag weighs over 50 pounds, add a heavy penalty of 50 dollars. If a bag weighs over 70 pounds, it is not allowed and incurs a flat 200 dollar penalty instead of standard fees. Passengers with elite status get their first bag free and waive the heavy penalty for all bags up to 70 pounds. Return a list of total fees per passenger. For example, given [("elite", 200, [40, 60])], standard fees would be 30 and 40, but elite waives the first bag and the heavy penalty on the second, resulting in a return of [40].

title: Streaming Royalty Distribution
spec: `royalties(streams)` processes a list of song stream records containing total plays, premium user plays, and artist tier. Calculate the payout for each song. Premium streams pay out at 0.015 per play. Ad supported streams, which are total plays minus premium plays, pay out at 0.005 per play. If the artist tier is top, they receive a 20 percent bonus on total payout. If the artist tier is emerging and their total plays exceed 50000, they get a flat 100 bonus. Deduct a 5 percent administrative fee from the final amount for all tiers. Return a list of payouts rounded to three decimals. For example, given [(100000, 40000, "emerging")], premium pays 600 and ad supported pays 300, plus a 100 bonus, less a 5 percent fee, returning [950.0].

title: Cinema Seating Group Allocation
spec: `seating(requests)` takes a list of requested group sizes to assign to a theater with 10 rows of 20 seats each. Assign seats starting from the back row down to the front. Within a row, fill seats from left to right. If a group cannot fit entirely within the remaining contiguous seats of a single row, they must be split, but try to place them in the next available row if it is completely empty. If no single empty row can hold them, split them across the current row and the next ones. Track the total number of groups successfully seated together without splitting, and the total number of individuals who could not be seated because the theater filled up. Return a tuple of these two numbers. For example, given [10, 5, 8], the first row easily fits 10 and 5, while 8 spills into the empty next row, keeping them together, returning (3, 0).

title: Greenhouse Climate Controller Actions
spec: `climate(sensors)` accepts a list of sensor readings where each is a tuple of temperature, humidity, and sunlight intensity. Determine the climate control actions for each reading. If temperature is below 15, trigger heating. If temperature is above 25 and humidity is below 40, trigger misting. If temperature is above 30, trigger venting regardless of humidity. If sunlight intensity is above 80 and temperature exceeds 28, trigger shading instead of venting to prevent scorch. If humidity is above 85, trigger dehumidifying unless heating is already active, in which case do nothing about humidity. Return a list of strings representing the primary action for each sensor reading, defaulting to standby. For example, given [(10, 50, 40)], it returns ["heating"].

title: Frequent Flyer Mile Accumulation
spec: `miles(flights)` takes a list of flight records where each is a tuple of distance, ticket class, and current frequent flyer tier. Calculate the earned miles for each flight. Base miles equal the distance flown. If ticket class is business, add a 50 percent bonus to base miles. If ticket class is first, add a 100 percent bonus. Then apply tier multipliers to total base and class miles: gold members get an extra 25 percent, platinum members get 50 percent, and diamond members get 100 percent. Flights under 500 distance earn a minimum of 500 base miles before class and tier bonuses are applied. Return a list of final miles rounded to the nearest integer. For example, given [(400, "economy", "basic")], it returns [500].

title: Veterinary Medication Dosage
spec: `dosage(animals)` takes a list of animal records containing species, weight in kilograms, and age in months. Calculate required medication dosage in milliliters. For dogs, the base dose is 2.0 milliliters per kilogram. For cats, the base dose is 1.5 milliliters per kilogram. For rabbits, it is 0.8 milliliters per kilogram. If the animal is under 6 months old, reduce the total dose by 30 percent to prevent toxicity. If the animal is over 120 months old, increase the dose by 10 percent due to slower absorption rates. The maximum allowable dose for any animal is 50 milliliters. Return a list of calculated dosages rounded to one decimal place. For example, given [("dog", 10.0, 4)], it calculates a base of 20.0 but applies a 30 percent reduction for age, returning [14.0].

title: Aquarium Tank Compatibility
spec: `aquarium(fish)` evaluates a list of proposed fish additions, where each fish is a tuple of species name, minimum temperature, maximum temperature, and aggression level. Determine if the group can share a single tank. First find the overlapping temperature range for all fish; if there is no common temperature where all can survive, the tank is invalid. Second check aggression levels: if any fish has an aggressive rating, there can be no fish with a peaceful rating in the same tank. Semi aggressive fish can coexist with both, but if there are more than 3 semi aggressive fish, the tank becomes invalid due to overcrowding stress. Return a tuple containing a boolean for validity and the calculated midpoint of the safe temperature range, or 0 if invalid. For example, given [("tetra", 20, 25, "peaceful"), ("betta", 24, 28, "aggressive")], it returns (False, 0).

title: Marathon Runner Pacing Strategy
spec: `pacing(segments)` takes a list of course segments where each has distance in kilometers, elevation gain in meters, and surface type. Calculate the estimated time in minutes for each segment. The base pace is 5.0 minutes per kilometer. For every 10 meters of elevation gain, add 15 seconds to the segment time. If the surface is trail, increase the total segment time by 20 percent. If the surface is sand, increase it by 40 percent. For downhill segments where elevation gain is negative, subtract 10 seconds per 10 meters of drop, but maximum speed gain is capped at 30 seconds per kilometer to prevent injury. Return a list of estimated minutes per segment rounded to two decimals. For example, given [(1.0, 20, "road")], it returns [5.5].

title: Real Estate Commission Splitter
spec: `commissions(sales)` processes a list of property sales containing sale price, listing agent name, and selling agent name. Calculate net earnings for each agent across all sales. Total commission is 6 percent of the sale price. This total is split evenly between listing and selling sides. If the same agent represents both sides, they receive the full 6 percent. The brokerage takes a 20 percent cut from each agent gross earnings per sale. Furthermore deduct a flat 150 dollar transaction fee from each agent net per sale. Return a list of tuples containing the agent name and their total accumulated net earnings across all transactions, sorted alphabetically by name. For example, given [(100000, "Alice", "Bob")], it returns [("Alice", 2250.0), ("Bob", 2250.0)].

title: Insurance Premium Risk Assessor
spec: `premiums(policies)` evaluates a list of auto insurance applicants containing age, years driving, number of accidents, and vehicle type. Calculate the annual premium for each. Base premium is 1000 dollars. If the driver is under 25, add a 400 dollar surcharge. If they have less than 3 years of driving experience, add 200 dollars. For each accident on record, increase the current total by 20 percent. If the vehicle type is sports, add a 500 dollar flat fee. If the vehicle is a minivan, apply a 10 percent discount to the final amount. Drivers over 65 with zero accidents get an additional senior discount of 150 dollars. Return a list of final premiums. For example, given [(30, 5, 0, "sedan")], it returns [1000.0].

title: Concert Ticket Scalper Detector
spec: `scalpers(purchases)` takes a list of purchase events containing buyer name, home address, and number of tickets bought. Identify suspicious buyers based on transaction patterns. A buyer is flagged if they purchase more than 8 tickets in a single transaction. They are also flagged if their cumulative ticket count across all transactions exceeds 15. Additionally if multiple different buyer names use the exact same home address, all buyers at that address are flagged for investigation. Finally if a buyer makes more than 3 separate transactions regardless of ticket count, they are flagged. Return a list of uniquely flagged buyer names sorted alphabetically. For example, given [("John", "123 Main St", 10)], it returns ["John"].

title: Recipe Calorie Macro Estimator
spec: `macros(ingredients)` accepts a list of ingredients where each is a tuple of name, weight in grams, protein per 100 grams, and fat per 100 grams. Calculate total calories and macronutrients for the entire recipe. Protein provides 4 calories per gram, and fat provides 9 calories per gram. For each ingredient, calculate its total protein and fat based on its weight. If the recipe involves baking, which is indicated if any ingredient is named flour, apply a 10 percent moisture loss to the total weight but keep calories the same. If an ingredient has more fat than protein, add a 20 percent calorie penalty to that ingredient to account for oil absorption during cooking. Return a tuple of total calories, total protein, and total fat, rounded to whole numbers. For example, given [("chicken", 200, 31, 3.6)], it returns (313, 62, 7).

title: Wind Chill and Heat Index
spec: `weather(readings)` processes a list of meteorological readings containing temperature in celsius, wind speed in kilometers per hour, and humidity percentage. Calculate perceived temperature for each. If temperature is 10 degrees or lower and wind speed is above 4.8, calculate wind chill by reducing temperature based on wind speed. If temperature is 27 degrees or higher and humidity is above 40 percent, calculate heat index by increasing temperature based on humidity level. For temperatures between 11 and 26 degrees inclusive, perceived temperature is equal to actual temperature. Return a list of perceived temperatures rounded to one decimal place. For example, given [(20, 10, 50)], it returns [20.0].

title: Spacecraft Payload Mass Budget
spec: `payload(components)` evaluates a list of spacecraft components where each contains name, base mass, and power draw in watts. Calculate total launch mass including necessary support systems. Structural mass is exactly 20 percent of the sum of all component base masses. For every 50 watts of total power draw, one solar panel is required, and each panel adds 5 kilograms. The thermal control system adds 2 kilograms for every 100 watts of total power draw. Finally a safety margin of 15 percent is added to the total mass of components, structure, panels, and thermal systems. Return the final budgeted mass rounded to the nearest integer. For example, given [("sensor", 10, 100)], it yields 28 after calculating base, structure, panels, thermal, and margin.

title: Toll Road Billing System
spec: `tolls(vehicles)` processes a list of vehicle records containing axle count, vehicle class, and distance traveled on the toll network. Calculate the toll charge for each vehicle. The base rate is 10 cents per mile traveled. Vehicles with more than 2 axles pay an extra 5 cents per mile for each additional axle. If the vehicle class is commercial, apply a 1.5 multiplier to the total distance charge. Emergency vehicles pay zero toll regardless of distance or axles. Electric vehicles receive a 20 percent discount on their final calculated toll to encourage green energy. Return a list of toll charges rounded to two decimals. For example, given [(2, "personal", 100)], it returns [10.0].

title: Mobile Data Plan Overage
spec: `data(usage)` accepts a list of user accounts containing base plan gigabytes, used gigabytes, and rollover gigabytes from the previous month. Calculate the monthly bill for each account. The base plan costs 10 dollars per gigabyte. Usage is first deducted from rollover gigabytes, then from the base plan. If total used gigabytes exceed the sum of base and rollover, the excess is billed at a premium overage rate of 20 dollars per gigabyte. Accounts that use less than 50 percent of their base plan receive a 5 dollar credit on their bill. Return a list of final bill amounts. For example, given [(10, 12, 5)], usage is fully covered by rollover and base, so it returns [100].

title: Cargo Ship Load Balancing
spec: `cargo(containers)` evaluates a list of container records containing weight in tons, destination port, and a boolean for hazardous materials. Determine deck placement for each container. Hazardous containers must be placed on the upper deck. Containers weighing over 30 tons must be placed in the lower hold to maintain stability. Regular containers under 30 tons go to the middle deck. If a container is both hazardous and over 30 tons, it is rejected and marked as invalid. Calculate total weight distributed to each of the three valid areas. Return a tuple of total weights for upper deck, middle deck, and lower hold. For example, given [(20, "NY", False)], it returns (0, 20, 0).

title: Online Grocery Delivery Fee
spec: `delivery(orders)` takes a list of order records containing cart total, distance to customer in miles, and requested delivery speed. Calculate the delivery fee for each order. Standard base fee is 5 dollars. If the distance is over 10 miles, add 1 dollar per additional mile. If the delivery speed is express, add a flat 8 dollar surcharge. If the cart total exceeds 100 dollars, the standard base fee and distance charges are waived, but the express surcharge still applies. Orders placed with a cart total under 20 dollars incur a small basket fee of 3 dollars. Return a list of final delivery fees. For example, given [(50, 5, "standard")], it returns [5].

title: Mining Extraction Yield
spec: `mining(samples)` takes a list of ore samples where each is a tuple of rock type, weight in tons, and mineral purity percentage. Calculate the extracted yield of precious metals in kilograms. First multiply weight by purity percentage to find gross mineral content. For quartz rock type, extraction efficiency is 90 percent. For granite, it is 70 percent due to harder crushing requirements. For shale, efficiency is 85 percent but incurs a flat deduction of 2 kilograms of yield for chemical processing losses. If calculated yield falls below zero, record it as zero. Return a list of net yields in kilograms. For example, given [("quartz", 100, 50)], it returns [45.0].

title: Server Rack Power Allocation
spec: `racks(servers)` accepts a list of server configurations containing unit size, cpu core count, and storage drive count. Calculate total power requirement in watts for each server. Baseline power for any server is 100 watts per unit size. Each cpu core adds 15 watts. Each storage drive adds 10 watts. If the server has more than 32 cores, it requires an auxiliary cooling fan which draws an additional 50 watts. If the unit size is 4 or larger, apply a 10 percent efficiency penalty to total power due to extended power bus lines. Return a list of calculated power requirements. For example, given [(2, 16, 4)], it returns [480.0].

title: Smart Home Lighting Schedule
spec: `lighting(events)` evaluates a list of room events containing room type, motion detected boolean, and natural light level percentage. Determine lighting status for each event. If motion is detected and natural light is below 40 percent, turn lights on to 100 percent brightness. If motion is detected but natural light is between 40 and 70 percent, turn lights on to 50 percent brightness to save energy. If no motion is detected for a hallway, turn lights to a dim 10 percent for safety. For all other rooms with no motion, or if natural light is above 70 percent, turn lights off. Return a list of brightness percentages. For example, given [("living room", True, 20)], it returns [100].

title: Ebook Formatting Cost
spec: `ebook(manuscripts)` takes a list of manuscript records containing word count, number of images, and a list of required output formats. Calculate the formatting fee for each manuscript. The base rate is 0.02 dollars per word. Each image adds 5 dollars for manual placement. Producing a standard digital format costs a flat 50 dollars. If a print ready format is requested in the output formats list, add 100 dollars. If the word count exceeds 100000, apply a 10 percent bulk discount to the entire total. Return a list of formatting fees rounded to two decimal places. For example, given [(50000, 10, ["digital"])], it returns [1100.0].

title: Fitness Challenge Leaderboard
spec: `fitness(participants)` processes a list of participant records containing name, a list of daily step counts, and total active minutes. Calculate total challenge score for each participant. Each step is worth 1 point. Each active minute is worth 10 points. If a participant averages more than 10000 steps per day across their provided counts, they receive a 5000 point bonus. If they have zero steps on any given day, they lose 1000 points as a consistency penalty. Return a list of tuples containing the participant name and their final score, sorted by score in descending order. For example, given [("Eve", [5000, 6000], 120)], it returns [("Eve", 12200)].

title: Cloud Storage Billing
spec: `storage(accounts)` takes a list of user storage records containing standard gigabytes, archive gigabytes, and number of read requests. Calculate the monthly storage bill. Standard storage costs 0.03 dollars per gigabyte. Archive storage costs 0.01 per gigabyte but charges 0.05 for every 100 read requests. If an account stores more than 1000 standard gigabytes, the rate drops to 0.02 per gigabyte for the standard portion. Free tier accounts, identified if total combined storage is under 5 gigabytes, pay zero dollars regardless of reads. Return a list of final bills rounded to two decimal places. For example, given [(10, 5, 200)], it returns [0.45].

title: Mastermind Peg Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(guesses, secret)` that returns a list of feedback tuples for a sequence of guess lists. Each guess and the secret are lists of colors. For each guess, count the number of exact matches where the color and position match. Then, count the number of partial matches where a color exists in the secret but in a different position, ensuring each peg in the secret is only matched once. Return a tuple of exact and partial match counts for each guess. For example, if the secret is red, blue, red, green and the guess is red, red, yellow, blue, the exact count is one and the partial count is two.

title: Gymnastics Execution Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(routines)` that calculates the final scores for a list of gymnastics routines. Each input tuple contains the starting difficulty value and a list of five execution scores from different judges. Sort the five execution scores from lowest to highest. Discard the single lowest and the single highest execution scores to prevent judge bias. Calculate the average of the remaining three execution scores. Deduct this average from ten to determine the execution deduction. Add the starting difficulty value to the resulting execution score to find the final routine score. Return a list of the final scores rounded to three decimal places.

title: Options Spread Profit Evaluator
spec: Write a function `profit(positions, price)` that calculates the total net profit or loss of an options portfolio at expiration. The positions input is a list of tuples detailing the option type which is either call or put, the position type which is long or short, the strike price, the premium paid or received, and the number of contracts. The price is the underlying asset price at expiration. For long calls, the payoff is the maximum of zero and the price minus strike. For short calls, it is the minimum of zero and the strike minus price. Compute the payoff for puts similarly, multiply by the contract amount and a multiplier of one hundred, and adjust by the initial premiums. Return the total monetary profit as a float.

title: Genetic Sequence Protein Translator
spec: Write a function `translate(sequence)` that converts a string of nucleotide characters into a list of amino acid strings. Scan the sequence to find the first start codon which is A U G. From there, read the sequence in chunks of three characters. Look up each triplet in a standard genetic code mapping to find the corresponding amino acid name. Stop translating if a stop codon such as U A A, U A G, or U G A is encountered. Ignore any remaining characters after the stop codon. If no start codon is found, return an empty list.

title: Decathlon Track and Field Scorer
spec: Write a function `calculate(performances)` that computes the total points for a decathlon athlete. The input is a list of tuples containing the event name and the performance metric, which is seconds for running and meters for throwing or jumping. Use the standard decathlon point formulas which involve three parameters per event. For track events, points are calculated based on a base parameter multiplied by the difference between a maximum time and the performance, raised to an exponent. For field events, points are the base parameter multiplied by the difference between the performance and a minimum distance, raised to an exponent. Truncate the points for each event to an integer before summing them to get the total score.

title: Drop Frame Timecode Adder
spec: Write a function `add(timecodes)` that sums a list of video timecode strings and returns the total as a single timecode string. Each input represents hours, minutes, seconds, and frames separated by colons. Assume a frame rate of thirty frames per second. Convert each timecode to a total frame count. To handle drop frame rules, subtract two frames for every minute except for minutes perfectly divisible by ten. Sum the total frames. Convert the total frame count back into hours, minutes, seconds, and frames, re-applying the drop frame logic to find the correct string representation. Return the final formatted timecode string.

title: Direct Mapped Cache Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(accesses, size, block)` that returns the number of cache hits and misses. The accesses input is a list of integer memory addresses. The size is the total number of bytes the cache can hold, and the block is the number of bytes per cache line. Calculate the number of sets by dividing the size by the block. For each memory address, compute its block address by dividing by the block size. Determine the cache index using the modulo operator with the number of sets. Maintain a record of the current block address stored at each cache index. Count a hit if the stored block matches the requested block, otherwise count a miss and update the stored block. Return a tuple of hits and misses.

title: Digital Line Rasterization Coordinates
spec: Write a function `rasterize(start, end)` that returns a list of integer coordinate tuples forming a line between two points. The start and end inputs are tuples of x and y coordinates. Implement the integer-only drawing algorithm to calculate the path. Determine the absolute differences in the x and y directions and the step direction for each axis, which is either positive or negative one. Initialize an error term based on the differences. Iterate from the starting coordinate, adding it to the result list, and update the coordinates by modifying the error term. Yield a continuous line of pixels until the end coordinate is reached and return the list.

title: Divide and Conquer Multiplication Tracer
spec: Write a function `multiply(x, y)` that multiplies two large integers and returns a tuple containing the final product and a list of intermediate multiplication steps. Convert the numbers to strings to determine the maximum length, then pad them with leading zeros to make their lengths equal and a power of two. Split each number into upper and lower halves. Recursively compute three products: the upper halves, the lower halves, and the sum of the halves. Append each pair of numbers being multiplied at the base case to the steps list. Combine the recursive results using appropriate powers of ten to form the final result.

title: Shortest Processing Time Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(jobs)` that returns the optimal order of jobs to minimize average completion time. The input is a list of tuples containing a job identifier, arrival time, and processing time. Track the current time and a list of waiting jobs. Advance the current time to the next arrival if the waiting list is empty. Move jobs that have arrived by the current time into the waiting list. Select the job with the smallest processing time from the waiting list to execute next. Add its identifier to the output list and advance the current time by its processing time. Repeat until all jobs are processed.

title: Dual Tone Multi Frequency Decoder
spec: Write a function `decode(frequencies)` that translates a list of frequency pairs into a string of telephone keypad characters. Each input tuple contains a low frequency and a high frequency in hertz. Compare the low frequency to the standard row frequencies with a tolerance of five percent to identify the row. Compare the high frequency to the standard column frequencies with the same tolerance to identify the column. Map the identified row and column to the corresponding button which is a digit, star, or pound sign. If a frequency pair falls outside the acceptable tolerance for any standard tone, append a question mark to the result. Return the final decoded string.

title: English to Braille Translator
spec: Write a function `translate(text)` that converts an English string into a sequence of Braille cell representations. Represent each Braille cell as a six-character string of dots and dashes, corresponding to the two columns of three dots. Map lowercase letters to their standard patterns. For uppercase letters, prepend a special capitalization cell before the lowercase pattern. Map digits to the letters A through J, but prepend a special number indicator cell before sequences of digits. For spaces, use a cell of six dashes. Return a list of all the generated cell strings in order.

title: Dead Reckoning Navigation Tracer
spec: Write a function `trace(origin, movements)` that calculates the final geographic coordinate after a series of movements. The origin is a tuple of starting latitude and longitude. The movements input is a list of tuples containing a heading in degrees, speed in knots, and duration in hours. For each movement, convert the heading to radians and compute the distance traveled by multiplying speed and duration. Calculate the change in latitude and longitude using trigonometric functions, adjusting for the Earth radius. Keep a running sum of the coordinates. Return the final coordinate as a tuple rounded to four decimal places.

title: Julian to Gregorian Date Converter
spec: Write a function `convert(dates)` that translates a list of historical date tuples into their Gregorian equivalents. Each input tuple contains a year, month, and day. Check if the date falls before the historical switch in October fifteen eighty-two. If it does, calculate the number of leap years under the old system and compare it to the new system rules, where century years are not leap years unless divisible by four hundred. Determine the exact number of days to shift based on the century. Add this shift to the day, rolling over months and years if the day exceeds the days in that month. Return a list of adjusted date tuples.

title: Naval Semaphore Flag Decoder
spec: Write a function `decode(angles)` that converts a list of flag angle pairs into a readable message. Each input tuple contains two angles in degrees representing the positions of the left and right flags. Snap the angles to the nearest multiple of forty-five degrees. Compare the pair of snapped angles to the standard semaphore alphabet dictionary, which maps angle pairs to letters. If the pair matches the special numerical shift signal, treat subsequent letters as numbers until an alphabetical shift signal is found. Ignore identical consecutive angle pairs as they represent a pause. Return the final decoded string.

title: Grayscale Halftone Dot Generator
spec: Write a function `halftone(pixels, width, height)` that converts a flat list of grayscale values into a pattern of varying dot sizes. Iterate over the image in blocks of two by two pixels. Calculate the average grayscale value for each block. Map this average, which ranges from zero to two hundred fifty-five, to a dot size ranging from zero to four. Append a character representation for the dot size to a line string, using blank spaces, periods, lower case o, upper case O, and an at symbol for the darkest blocks. Add a line break after reaching the width divided by two. Return the final multiline string.

title: Damped Harmonic Oscillator Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(mass, spring, damping, steps)` that traces the position of a mass on a spring over time. The mass, spring constant, and damping coefficient are floats, and steps is an integer number of time intervals. Start with an initial displacement of ten and an initial velocity of zero. Use a time step of zero point one seconds. For each step, calculate the spring force and the damping force. Find the acceleration by dividing the total force by the mass. Update the velocity using the acceleration, and then update the displacement using the velocity. Return a list of the displacement values at each step.

title: Telephone Number Prefix Parser
spec: Write a function `parse(numbers)` that normalizes a list of phone number strings and extracts their country details. Strip all spaces, dashes, and parentheses from each number. Check if the number starts with a plus sign. If so, match the following digits against a list of known international calling codes to find the country. If there is no plus sign, assume it is a local domestic number. Format the parsed result as a tuple containing the country name and the remaining local subscriber digits. If an international code is unrecognized, use the word unknown for the country. Return a list of these tuples.

title: Saffir Simpson Hurricane Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(measurements)` that evaluates wind speed data over time to determine hurricane categories. The input is a list of maximum sustained wind speeds in knots recorded every six hours. Convert each wind speed to miles per hour. Compare the speed to the Saffir-Simpson thresholds to classify the storm from a tropical depression up to a category five hurricane. Keep track of the highest category reached so far. Construct a list of tuples containing the time index, the current classification, and a boolean indicating whether the storm has upgraded to a new maximum intensity at this time step. Return the list.

title: International Shoe Size Converter
spec: Write a function `convert(sizes)` that translates a list of local shoe size numbers into European, British, and Japanese equivalents. Each input size is an American men size as a float. To find the European size, add thirty-three to the American size. For the British size, subtract one from the American size. For the Japanese size in centimeters, add eighteen to the American size. Round all results to the nearest half size. If an input size is less than six or greater than sixteen, append a string indicating it is out of bounds instead of the sizes. Return a list of tuples containing the three translated sizes or the error string.

title: Postal Routing Barcode Generator
spec: Write a function `generate(zipcodes)` that converts a list of five-digit zip code strings into postal routing barcodes. First, calculate a correction digit for each zip code so that the sum of all six digits is a multiple of ten. For each of the six digits, use a standard mapping to translate the number into a pattern of five tall and short bars, where exactly two bars are tall. Prepend a single tall frame bar at the very beginning of the pattern. Append another single tall frame bar at the very end. Return a list of the full barcode strings consisting of tall and short characters.

title: Web Pagination Range Generator
spec: Write a function `paginate(current, total, siblings)` that returns a list of page numbers and truncation symbols for a web pagination control. The current page, total pages, and siblings count are integers. Always include the first page and the last page. Include a range of pages around the current page, determined by the siblings count on the left and right. If there is a gap of more than one page between the first page and the start of the sibling range, insert an ellipsis string. Do the same if there is a gap between the end of the sibling range and the last page. Return the list of integers and ellipsis strings.

title: Radio Frequency Spectrum Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(requests)` that assigns radio frequency bands to a list of broadcast stations. The input is a list of tuples containing the station identifier and requested bandwidth in megahertz. Maintain a list of available frequency ranges, initially one large block from eighty-eight to one hundred eight megahertz. For each request, find the first available block that is at least as large as the requested bandwidth plus a guard band of point two megahertz. Assign the lower portion of the block to the station and update the remaining available block. Return a list of tuples with the station identifier and assigned starting and ending frequencies.

title: Camera Exposure Value Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(settings)` that determines the exposure value for a list of camera shots. Each input tuple contains the aperture f-stop as a float, the shutter speed as a fraction string like one over two hundred, and the ISO sensitivity as an integer. Convert the shutter speed string into a decimal float. Calculate the base exposure value using the base two logarithm of the aperture squared divided by the shutter speed. Adjust this base value for the ISO by subtracting the base two logarithm of the ISO divided by one hundred. Return a list of the final exposure values rounded to one decimal place.

title: Blood Pressure Reading Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify(readings)` that evaluates a list of patient blood pressure tuples. Each tuple contains a systolic and diastolic integer pressure. Compare the numbers against standard medical thresholds. Categorize as normal if systolic is under one hundred twenty and diastolic is under eighty. If systolic is between one hundred twenty and one hundred twenty-nine and diastolic is under eighty, categorize as elevated. If systolic is up to one hundred thirty-nine or diastolic is up to eighty-nine, it is stage one hypertension. Higher numbers mean stage two, and if systolic exceeds one hundred eighty or diastolic exceeds one hundred twenty, it is a hypertensive crisis. Return a list of the category strings.

title: Ski Jumping Score Calculator
spec: The function `evaluate(jumps)` processes a list of jumps, where each jump is a tuple containing the jump distance in meters, the hill critical point in meters, a list of five style judge scores, a wind compensation number, and a starting gate adjustment factor. The base distance score starts at sixty points for reaching the critical point exactly. For every meter beyond or short of the critical point, add or subtract one point eight points. Next, discard the highest and lowest style judge scores, and sum the remaining three to get the style total. Add this style total to the distance score. Then, apply the gate compensation by adding or subtracting its value directly. Finally, add the wind compensation number, which may be negative. If the final total is less than zero, adjust it to zero. Return a list of the final scores rounded to one decimal place.

title: Cribbage Show Phase Evaluator
spec: The function `evaluate(cards)` calculates the point value of a five card cribbage hand. The input is a list of five string tuples, each representing a rank and a suit, where the last card represents the starter card. First, calculate points for fifteens by finding all combinations of cards whose values exactly sum to fifteen, scoring two points for each combination. Face cards count as ten and aces as one. Next, find all pairs of cards with the exact same rank, scoring two points per pair. Then, look for runs of three or more consecutive ranks and score one point per card in the longest run. After that, check if all four cards in the player hand share the same suit for a four point flush, and add a fifth point if the starter card also matches. Finally, add one point if the hand contains a jack matching the suit of the starter card. Return the total score as an integer.

title: Board Game Word Scorer
spec: The function `calculate(plays)` computes the scores for a list of played words on a grid. The input is a list of plays, where each play is a string of uppercase letters, and optionally a list of premium square indicators for each letter position such as double letter, triple letter, double word, or triple word. First, map each letter to its standard English tile value, assigning zero if it is a blank tile. For each letter, multiply its value by two or three if a letter premium applies at that position. Sum these base values to get the initial word score. Next, count the number of word premiums and multiply the entire word score by two or three for each double or triple word indicator present. If the word length is exactly seven letters, add a fifty point bonus. Finally, subtract a five point penalty if the word contains more than two vowels. Return a list of integer scores for each play.

title: Grand Prix Race Scorer
spec: The function `rank(results)` calculates the championship points for a single motor racing weekend. The input is a list of driver results, where each result is a tuple containing a driver name, their sprint race finish position, their main race finish position, and a boolean indicating if they drove the fastest lap. For the sprint race, award eight points for first place, down to one point for eighth place, with zero points for ninth or lower. For the main race, award twenty five points for first, eighteen for second, fifteen for third, and a standard sliding scale down to one point for tenth. If a driver recorded the fastest lap, award one additional point, but only if their main race finish position was tenth or better. If a driver failed to finish either race, indicated by a position of zero, deduct two penalty points from their weekend total. Sum all points for each driver and return a list of tuples containing the driver name and their total points, sorted by points in descending order.

title: French Tarot Hand Scorer
spec: The function `tally(cards)` determines the points in a player pile for the card game Tarot, and the target score needed to fulfill their contract. The input is a list of cards where each card is a string indicating its rank and suit, or a special trump. First, count the number of special trumps known as oudlers, which are the one of trumps, the twenty one of trumps, and the excuse. Based on the oudler count, determine the target score: fifty six points for zero oudlers, fifty one for one, forty one for two, and thirty six for three. Next, sum the card values. Kings and oudlers are worth four and a half points, queens are three and a half, knights are two and a half, jacks are one and a half, and all other basic cards are half a point. If the total card points exceed seventy five, cap the recorded total at seventy five to prevent accounting errors. Return a tuple containing the total card points as a float and the required target score.

title: Exoplanet Transit Analyzer
spec: The function `analyze(lightcurves)` processes a list of astronomical brightness measurements to detect planetary transits. The input is a list of tuples containing time in days, measured stellar flux, and a background noise level. First, establish a baseline flux by averaging the measurements from the first and last quarters of the dataset. Normalize the entire dataset by dividing all flux values by this baseline. Next, scan the normalized data to find the minimum flux value, representing the maximum transit depth. Calculate the planetary radius relative to the star by taking the square root of the transit depth. Determine the duration of the transit by counting consecutive time points where the flux remains below a ninety nine percent threshold of the baseline. If the background noise level during the transit exceeds five percent of the baseline, mark the detection as unconfirmed by setting the radius to zero. Return a tuple with the relative radius and transit duration.

title: Seismic Event Triangulator
spec: The function `locate(stations)` estimates the distance to an earthquake epicenter based on seismic wave arrival times. The input is a list of stations, where each station is a tuple containing the station name, the arrival time of the primary compression wave, and the arrival time of the secondary shear wave in seconds. For each station, compute the time difference between the secondary and primary wave arrivals. Because primary waves travel faster, use the time difference to estimate the distance to the epicenter by multiplying the delay by a constant factor of eight point four kilometers per second. If the calculated distance is less than ten kilometers, classify it as a shallow local event by applying a one point one multiplier to the distance to account for crustal reflection. Next, identify the station with the shortest calculated distance to find the nearest observation point. Return a list of tuples with the station name and calculated distance, followed by the name of the nearest station.

title: Volcanic Ash Plume Estimator
spec: The function `estimate(eruptions)` calculates the expected maximum height of a volcanic ash plume. The input is a list of eruptions, where each eruption provides the mass eruption rate in kilograms per second, the atmospheric temperature profile gradient, and the crosswind velocity at the vent in meters per second. First, convert the mass eruption rate into a buoyancy flux by multiplying it by a specific heat capacity constant and dividing by the reference air density and temperature. If the mass eruption rate is extremely low, below one thousand kilograms per second, assume the plume collapses immediately and set the height to zero. For larger eruptions, check the crosswind. If the crosswind is less than five meters per second, model the plume as wind free and calculate the height proportional to the fourth root of the buoyancy flux. If the crosswind is stronger, treat it as a bent over plume and calculate the height using a cube root scaling law adjusted by the wind speed. Return a list of the estimated heights converted to kilometers.

title: Concrete Curing Strength Predictor
spec: The function `predict(batches)` estimates the compressive strength of concrete over time based on its mix and curing environment. The input is a list of batches, each containing the water to cement ratio, the curing time in days, and the average ambient temperature in Celsius. First, establish a base strength at twenty eight days by applying Abrams law, which takes a structural constant of ninety five divided by an empirical constant raised to the power of the water to cement ratio. Next, calculate a maturity index by multiplying the curing days by the ambient temperature plus ten degrees. If the ambient temperature dropped below zero at any point, apply a permanent twenty percent penalty to the final predicted strength due to ice crystal damage. Apply a logarithmic growth function to the maturity index to find the strength development factor, and multiply the base strength by this factor. Finally, cap the maximum possible strength at one hundred and twenty percent of the base strength. Return a list of predicted strengths in megapascals.

title: Optical Fiber Attenuation Calculator
spec: The function `measure(links)` calculates the total signal loss in decibels across various fiber optic networks. The input is a list of link segments, each containing the fiber length in kilometers, the operating wavelength in nanometers, the number of fusion splices, and the number of connector pairs. First, determine the intrinsic fiber attenuation coefficient: use zero point two decibels per kilometer for a fifteen fifty nanometer wavelength, or zero point three five for thirteen ten nanometers, and multiply this by the length. Next, add splice losses by multiplying the number of splices by an average loss of zero point one decibels each. Then, account for connector loss by multiplying the connector pairs by zero point seventy five decibels each. For long haul links exceeding fifty kilometers, add an extra erbium doped fiber amplifier insertion penalty of two decibels. Finally, add a systemic safety margin of one point five decibels for aging and temperature variations. Return a list of total loss values.

title: Submarine Ballast Flood Timer
spec: The function `flood(tanks)` calculates the time required to flood a submarine ballast tank to achieve neutral buoyancy. The input is a list of tanks, where each tank is a tuple of the tank volume in cubic meters, the diameter of the flood valve in meters, and the current dive depth in meters. First, calculate the cross sectional area of the valve using the diameter. Next, calculate the external water pressure based on the depth, assuming an increase of one atmosphere for every ten meters of depth. If the submarine is at the surface, depth is zero, so assume a minimal trickle flow rate of zero point one cubic meters per second instead of using theorem calculations. Otherwise, use Torricelli theorem to find the initial velocity of the incoming water, which is the square root of two times gravity times the depth. Compute the volumetric flow rate by multiplying the water velocity by the valve area and a discharge coefficient of zero point six. Divide the tank volume by the flow rate to find the flood time. Return a list of times in seconds.

title: Spacecraft Re-entry Heat Estimator
spec: The function `simulate(trajectories)` evaluates the peak heating rate experienced by a spacecraft returning to Earth. The input is a list of trajectory points, each containing the current altitude in kilometers, velocity in meters per second, and the nose radius of the spacecraft in meters. First, calculate the atmospheric density at the given altitude using an exponential atmosphere model, where sea level density decays based on a scale height of eight point five kilometers. Next, determine the stagnation point heat flux using the Sutton Graves equation, multiplying the square root of the density by the velocity cubed, and dividing by the square root of the nose radius. For velocities exceeding eleven point two kilometers per second, add a radiative heating component proportional to the fourth power of the velocity. Finally, apply a material specific scaling factor for the ablative shield, reducing the effective heat rate by fifteen percent. If the altitude is above one hundred kilometers, assume zero heat. Return a list of heat fluxes in watts per square centimeter.

title: English Snooker Break Evaluator
spec: The function `score(shots)` calculates the total points accumulated during a single continuous turn in snooker. The input is a list of strings representing consecutive potted balls by their color. The rules require alternating between potting a red ball, worth one point, and any of the six colored balls. After a colored ball is potted, the sequence must return to red until all fifteen reds are exhausted. The colored balls are valued from two points for yellow up to seven points for black. If the sequence violates the alternating rule while reds are on the table, immediately terminate the break calculation at that point and record the score up to the violation. Once all reds are gone, the remaining colored balls must be potted in strict ascending order of their point value. If any colored ball is potted out of order at the end, halt the calculation. Return the total valid score up to the first error as an integer.

title: Tabletop RPG Attribute Roller
spec: The function `roll(characters)` generates the six core ability scores for a list of new player characters. The input is a list of character class names as strings. For each character, simulate rolling four six sided dice for each of the six attributes: strength, dexterity, constitution, intelligence, wisdom, and charisma. For each attribute, identify the lowest die roll and discard it, summing the remaining three dice to get a score between three and eighteen. Once all six attributes are generated, check the total sum of the modifiers. Modifiers are calculated by subtracting ten from the score and dividing by two, rounding down. If the sum of all six modifiers is less than zero, or if the highest individual score is less than thirteen, the array is considered too weak, so reroll the entire character. Finally, if the class name is a spellcaster, swap the highest rolled attribute into the intelligence slot. Return a list of tuples containing the final six scores for each character.

title: Trading Card Booster Pack Generator
spec: The function `generate(sets)` simulates the creation of standard fifteen card booster packs for a trading card game. The input is a tuple of four lists representing a specific card set: a list of common cards, a list of uncommon cards, a list of rare cards, and a list of mythic cards. For each pack to be generated, first randomly select ten distinct cards from the common list. Next, randomly select three distinct cards from the uncommon list. For the rare slot, use a random chance to determine if it should be a rare or a mythic card, with mythics appearing exactly one in every eight packs. Then, add a standard basic land card. If a special foil premium card is randomly triggered, which happens in exactly one out of six packs, replace one of the previously chosen common cards with a random card drawn from any of the four rarity lists. Return a list of ten generated booster packs, where each pack is a list of card names.

title: Hexagon Board Resource Distributor
spec: The function `distribute(rolls)` determines the resources gathered by players after the dice are rolled in a settlement building board game. The input is a list of dice rolls between two and twelve, and a list of settlements. Each settlement is a tuple containing the player color, a boolean indicating if it is an upgraded city, and a list of adjacent terrain hexes, where each hex is a tuple of its resource type and its production number. Iterate through each dice roll. If the roll is exactly seven, instead of producing resources, subtract one resource from the running total of any player who has a settlement adjacent to a desert hex. Otherwise, iterate through all settlements and check their adjacent hexes. If a hex production number matches the dice roll, the player receives that resource. Regular settlements receive one resource unit, while upgraded cities receive two. Accumulate the total resources gathered across all rolls. Return a list of tuples detailing the player color, the resource type, and the total quantity received.

title: Reverse Osmosis Energy Calculator
spec: The function `evaluate(plants)` estimates the electrical energy consumption of reverse osmosis desalination plants. The input is a list of plant configurations, each containing the feed water salinity in parts per million, the daily product water volume in cubic meters, and the recovery rate percentage. First, calculate the osmotic pressure of the seawater by multiplying the salinity by a temperature specific constant of zero point zero seven five. Next, determine the required pump pressure by adding a membrane resistance factor of fifteen bars to the osmotic pressure, and then dividing by the recovery rate to account for concentration polarization. Calculate the hydraulic energy needed by multiplying the required pressure by the product volume. If the feed water salinity is below ten thousand, classify it as brackish water and bypass the energy recovery device entirely. Otherwise, reduce the hydraulic energy by thirty percent using an energy recovery turbine. Finally, adjust for a high pressure pump efficiency of eighty percent. Return a list of daily energy consumption values.

title: Interferometry Array Resolution Calculator
spec: The function `resolve(arrays)` calculates the angular resolution of various radio telescope networks. The input is a list of arrays, where each array is a tuple containing the maximum baseline length between two antennas in kilometers and the observing frequency in gigahertz. First, convert the observing frequency into the observation wavelength in meters by dividing the speed of light by the frequency in hertz. Next, convert the maximum baseline length from kilometers into meters. Calculate the theoretical angular resolution in radians by dividing the wavelength by the baseline length. Convert this resolution from radians into milliarcseconds by multiplying by two hundred and six million two hundred and sixty five thousand. If the array operates at a very low frequency, below one gigahertz, apply an ionospheric scattering blur factor by adding ten milliarcseconds to the final resolution. Finally, apply a twenty percent atmospheric degradation penalty for any frequencies above twenty gigahertz. Return a list of effective resolutions in milliarcseconds.

title: Planar Truss Member Force Calculator
spec: The function `calculate(trusses)` estimates the tension and compression forces on the internal members of a simple bridge truss. The input is a list of truss configurations, each containing the total span length in meters, the height of the truss in meters, and a point load applied at the center bottom node in kilonewtons. First, calculate the reaction forces at the two end supports, which due to symmetry will each hold exactly half of the applied center load. Next, use the span and height to find the angle of the diagonal members using inverse tangent geometry. Determine the force in the bottom horizontal chord by multiplying the reaction force by the length of a single panel, and dividing by the truss height. Calculate the force along the diagonal members by dividing the reaction force by the sine of the diagonal angle. Additionally, calculate the safety factor by dividing the steel yield strength of two hundred and fifty megapascals by the highest stress found in any member. Return a list of tuples containing the horizontal chord tension and the safety factor.

title: Aircraft Ground Roll Distance Estimator
spec: The function `compute(aircraft)` computes the runway distance required for airplanes to reach liftoff speed. The input is a list of aircraft conditions, each containing the aircraft mass in kilograms, engine thrust in newtons, wing area in square meters, and a lift coefficient. First, calculate the liftoff speed, which is one point two times the stall speed, determined by equating the lift formula to the aircraft weight using standard sea level air density. Next, estimate the average acceleration during the ground roll. Subtract the rolling resistance, assuming a friction coefficient of zero point zero two times the weight, and subtract the average aerodynamic drag from the engine thrust. Divide this net forward force by the aircraft mass to find acceleration. If the takeoff is from a wet runway, increase the rolling friction coefficient to zero point zero four. If the aircraft mass exceeds fifty thousand kilograms, add a ten percent safety margin to the final calculated distance. Return a list of takeoff distances in meters.

title: Lithium Ion Cycle Life Estimator
spec: The function `predict(batteries)` predicts the number of charge cycles a battery can endure before degrading to eighty percent of its original capacity. The input is a list of usage profiles, each containing the depth of discharge percentage, the average operating temperature in Celsius, and the charge cutoff voltage. First, establish a baseline lifespan of four thousand cycles for a standard twenty percent depth of discharge at twenty five degrees Celsius. Apply a depth of discharge penalty factor, halving the expected cycles for every additional twenty percent of discharge depth beyond the baseline. Next, account for temperature degradation by reducing the cycle count by five percent for every degree above twenty five Celsius, or by two percent for every degree below fifteen Celsius. If the usage profile includes fast charging, subtract an additional flat five hundred cycles from the total due to thermal stress. Finally, reduce the remaining lifespan by thirty percent if the charge cutoff voltage exceeds four point one volts. Return a list of expected cycle counts.

title: Scuba Decompression Stop Planner
spec: The function `plan(dives)` generates a safe ascent profile and required decompression stops for a scuba diver. The input is a list of dive profiles, each containing the maximum depth in meters, the bottom time in minutes, and the starting surface atmospheric pressure. First, calculate the ambient pressure at the maximum depth by adding the surface pressure to the depth divided by ten. Next, estimate the nitrogen tissue loading by multiplying the bottom time by the ambient pressure and a gas absorption constant. For dives made at high altitude, indicated by a starting surface pressure less than one atmosphere, reduce the safe surfacing threshold to twenty units. If the total nitrogen load remains below the surfacing threshold, no decompression stops are needed, and the diver ascends directly at a rate of nine meters per minute. If the load exceeds the threshold, calculate mandatory stops: a three minute safety stop at six meters, and a deep stop at half the maximum depth for every ten units of excess nitrogen. Return a list of total ascent times in minutes.

title: Solar Panel Yield Degradation
spec: The function `calculate(panels)` computes the lifetime energy production of a solar panel array factoring in environmental degradation. The input is a list of panel installations, each containing the rated capacity in watts, the age in years, and the climate type as a string. First, calculate the first year production by multiplying the capacity by an average of five peak sun hours per day and three hundred and sixty five days. Subtract a fixed two percent from this initial total to account for immediate light induced degradation. For each subsequent year up to the given age, reduce the previous year yield by an annual degradation rate. Set this rate to zero point five percent for moderate climates, zero point eight percent for hot climates, and one point two percent for arid desert climates due to thermal cycling. If it is a commercial scale panel over four hundred watts, assume superior manufacturing and reduce the annual degradation rate by zero point one percent. Sum the yields of all years to find the lifetime energy. Return a list of total energy values.

title: Asteroid Impact Crater Simulator
spec: The function `simulate(impactors)` estimates the diameter of the crater formed by an asteroid striking Earth. The input is a list of impactors, each containing the asteroid diameter in meters, its density in kilograms per cubic meter, its impact velocity in kilometers per second, and the impact angle in degrees. First, calculate the mass of the spherical asteroid using its diameter and density. Convert the impact velocity to meters per second to calculate the total kinetic energy of the impact in joules. Adjust this energy based on the impact angle by multiplying it by the sine of the angle, since shallow impacts transfer less energy to the ground. Apply a scaling law that relates the adjusted kinetic energy to the volume of displaced rock, assuming a standard crust density of three thousand. If the impact occurs over a deep ocean, defined as an impact angle greater than eighty degrees and a density below two thousand, reduce the displaced rock volume by thirty percent due to water dampening. Extract the final crater diameter from the displaced volume by assuming a bowl shape. Return a list of crater diameters in kilometers.

title: Acoustic Transmission Loss Evaluator
spec: The function `evaluate(walls)` calculates the sound transmission class of different wall assemblies. The input is a list of wall partitions, each containing the mass of the wall per square meter, the cavity depth in millimeters, a boolean indicating if fiberglass insulation is present, and a boolean for staggered studs. First, compute the basic mass law transmission loss at five hundred hertz, which scales logarithmically by taking twenty times the base ten logarithm of the surface mass, minus a constant of forty seven decibels. Next, determine the mass air mass resonance frequency using the cavity depth and the surface mass of the two wall panels. If this resonance frequency falls below one hundred hertz, add a five decibel penalty to the overall loss due to low frequency flanking. If fiberglass insulation is present in the cavity, add eight decibels to the total transmission loss to account for acoustic dampening. Finally, if the partition uses staggered wooden studs, which reduces structural bridging, add an extra three decibels to the final rating. Return a list of the final sound transmission class ratings as integers.

title: Sailboat Regatta Scoring
spec: Entry function `score(results)`. Input is a list of player performances, where each performance is a list of finishing positions represented as numbers or plain strings for did not start or disqualified. The logic must calculate total penalty points using a low point system where first place gets one point, second gets two, and so on. Any string entry receives points equal to the number of competitors plus one. If a player completes more than four races, discard their worst score. If they complete more than eight races, discard their two worst scores. Break ties by comparing the count of first place finishes, then second place finishes. Return a sorted list of total points. Example: inputting a player with finishes one, two, did not start, four, five should evaluate the string to six points, discard the six because there are five races, yielding a total of twelve.

title: Bicycle Spoke Length Calculator
spec: Entry function `spokes(dimensions)`. Input is a tuple containing rim diameter, hub diameter, hub width, cross pattern number, and total spoke count. The logic must calculate the straight line distance between the hub flange and the rim hole. It involves converting both diameters to radii, calculating the angle between spokes by dividing the cross pattern by the spoke count and multiplying by four pi. Next, use the law of cosines to find the two dimensional base length on the wheel plane. Apply the pythagorean theorem combining this base length and half the hub width to account for the lateral offset. Finally, subtract one millimeter to account for spoke stretch under tension. Return the length rounded to one decimal place. Example: an input of six hundred, forty, fifty, three, and thirty two should yield a spoke length around two hundred ninety two point five.

title: Cryptocurrency Tax FIFO Calculator
spec: Entry function `gains(transactions)`. Input is a chronological list of transaction tuples containing the operation type as a string, amount of coins, and price per coin. The operation type is either buy or sell. The logic must track capital gains using a first in first out method. It should maintain a queue of available purchase lots. When a sell occurs, it must be matched against the oldest available buys. If the sell amount exceeds the oldest buy, the buy is fully exhausted and the remaining sell amount applies to the next oldest buy. The profit is the difference between the sell price and the original buy price for each matched portion. Return the total accumulated profit. Example: buying two at ten, buying one at twenty, then selling two at thirty should match against the first buy entirely, yielding a profit of forty.

title: Water Polo Match Statistics
